title: Serve Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B, a 2.4T-Parameter Model, with Configurable Reasoning on NVIDIA GB300 NVL72
abstract: Alibaba released the open weights for Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B (Qwen3.8-Max), its largest open-weight model, bringing near-frontier capabilities to the open ecosystem. It has 2.4T total parameters with 95B activated per token. It has 2.4T total parameters with 95B activated per token. It’s a fine-grained mixture of experts (MoE) architecture with a hybrid of full and linear attention, a context window of up to one million tokens, and an output length of up to 128K, designed for demanding reasoning and agentic workloads. Deploying a 2.4T parameter open-weight model requires data-center-scale accelerated compute. Inference at this scale depends on extreme co-design across chips, system architecture, and software. NVIDIA is working with the open-source ecosystem to bring the model to multinode deployments through optimized kernels, inference runtimes, and distributed serving recipes. Without additional model tuning, the model achieves a throughput of over 4K tokens per second per GPU and over 350 tokens per second per user on NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 in FP8 precision on Day 0. Further optimizations, including NVFP4 precision, are expected to deliver enhanced performance gains over time. Architectural innovations for long-context inference Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B is built for the hardest agentic workloads like coding, large-scale document analysis, and long-running multi-step workflows. Unlike chat-first models that send a single prompt and receive a single reply, agentic applications accumulate system instructions, tool outputs, retrieved documents, code, logs, and multi-step reasoning traces across a workflow. As context grows, attention, compute, and KV cache memory become the binding constraints. The full-attention and linear-attention hybrid architecture addresses this, and the model alternates between the two. In the full-attention layers, every token attends to every other token, and in the linear-attention layers, the growing KV cache is replaced with a bounded recurrent state. Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B keeps both compute and memory bounded as context scales to up to one million tokens. Fine-grained MoE makes the 2.4T parameter count practical to serve. Instead of a small number of large experts, capacity is distributed across a larger population of smaller experts, improving specialization and routing efficiency per unit of activated compute. A learned router activates only the experts needed per token, so serving costs track active parameters, not the full 2.4T parameters, delivering frontier-scale capacity at a fraction of the cost of a comparable dense model. Built-in reasoning controls (low/high/xhigh) enable developers to configure inference depth per request, trading compute for reasoning quality depending on the task: dial up for complex multi-step reasoning or dial down for high-throughput document processing. Figure 1. Overview of the Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B linear gated delta networks plus full attention with fine-grained MoE architecture Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B optimized performance on GB300 NVL72 The GB300 NVL72 features a rack-scale architecture that integrates 72 NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra GPUs into a single platform. Its large, 72-GPU NVIDIA NVLink domain enables efficient all-to-all communication at 130 TB/s, eliminating bottlenecks that appear when expert traffic must cross traditional off-the-shelf networks. Out of the box, Qwen3.8 2.4T-A95B running on NVIDIA Blackwell GB300 NVL72 delivers over 4K tokens per second per GPU and over 350 tokens per second per user , enabling AI factories to run large-parameter models in production at high throughput and low latency. Figure 2. A Pareto curve showing Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B achieving over 4K tokens per second per GPU at peak throughput on NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 Post-train Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B and choose a serving path NVIDIA supports multiple inference stacks to meet a variety of developer needs. SGLang , vLLM , and NVIDIA Dynamo provide open-source inference recipes for developers who require greater control over performance on the NVIDIA-accelerated platform. It’s also available to deploy via a model-free NVIDIA NIM , a single inference container that serves any supported model. Download the model weights and deploy on Day-0 to serve fine-tuned checkpoints, and scale to production. Developers can post-train the model for domain-specific use cases using NVIDIA NeMo AutoModel , a PyTorch-native fine-tuning library with Day-0 Hugging Face checkpoint support. Train directly on existing checkpoints without model conversion, with support for full SFT or memory-efficient LoRA fine-tuning. Get started with Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B Download Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B model weights from Hugging Face or ModelScope and deploy with a model-free NVIDIA NIM from NVIDIA NGC.

title: How to Choose Full-Stack Observability for NVIDIA AI Factories
abstract: AI infrastructure spans multiple layers, from compute and networking to storage, orchestration, and applications. When performance degrades, identifying the source can be difficult because a symptom observed at one layer may originate elsewhere in the stack. A full-stack observability strategy connects telemetry across these layers, helping infrastructure and operations teams detect problems, isolate their causes, and maintain reliable AI workloads. This post presents a practical observability framework for NVIDIA AI infrastructure and shows how to apply it to common monitoring and troubleshooting scenarios. Consider a distributed training job that is three days into execution. GPU utilization and queue wait times remain normal. After six hours of reduced throughput, the team traces the cause to a single InfiniBand link drifting into an elevated bit error rate. This is a classic gray failure . The hardware is degraded, but the system does not report it as “down.” AI training follows the bulk synchronous parallel (BSP) model. These tightly coupled systems are sensitive to stragglers: one slow rank holds back the job. Link-level retransmissions stall a single rank during synchronous collective operations such as NVIDIA Collective Communications Library (NCCL) all-reduce. Throughput then falls to the slowest rank, and the other ranks block. That is a cascading failure. You see this failure mode often in AI factories. The required telemetry typically already exists; the challenge is selecting the right signals from the right tools early enough to act. Operators do not need every metric from every product. They need a decision path that maps components to tools, tools to a concise alert set, and that alert set into a single triage dashboard. This post shows that path. You will learn how to: Enumerate the failure domains that must be observable before selecting software. Map AI infrastructure components to telemetry tools sources using a decision framework derived from NVIDIA DGX deployments. Apply the observability framework to an InfiniBand cluster. Reduce telemetry to a top-k alert set and correlate signals in a single triage dashboard. Keep detailed catalogs, protocol matrices, and per-tool enablement guides in product documentation. Here, you’ll focus on how to choose an observability stack. NVIDIA DGX and NVIDIA HGX deployments share the same observability surface, even when hardware configurations differ (Figure 1): Identify AI factory failure domains Figure 1. AI factory architecture Before selecting monitoring software, enumerate the domains in which silent failure consumes GPU hours: Platform health : Fans, PSUs, BMC, chassis, CPU, memory, local storage. GPU health and performance : Utilization, temperature, power, XID/ECC, and NVIDIA NVLink throughput. Fabric : InfiniBand or Ethernet link integrity, congestion, and switch/cable health; rack-scale NVLink where present. Cluster and jobs : Scheduling, reservations, idle allocated GPUs, queue wait. Inference services : Latency, success rate, and cache behavior when NVIDIA NIM microservices or similar services are in production. In complex systems, coverage gaps are rarely closed in one pass. They appear later, when latent failure modes show up under load . Analyzing those modes early shortens discovery. This analysis can help prevent failures from recurring under load. Map AI infrastructure components to telemetry tools Operations teams need a clear mapping from component to telemetry source. Table 1 maps NVIDIA Data Center GPU Manager (DCGM), NVIDIA System Management (NVSM), NVIDIA Unified Fabric Manager (UFM), NVIDIA NetQ, NVIDIA NMX, NVIDIA Base Command Manager (BCM), and NVIDIA Run:ai to those components. Green indicates full support for the domain; yellow indicates partial or indirect coverage. Use the framework to select the minimum tool set that eliminates coverage gaps. Component Redfish / IPMI DCGM NVSM UFM NetQ NMX BCM Run:ai NIM Base infrastructure 🟢 ⚪ ⚪ ⚪ ⚪ ⚪ 🟢 ⚪ ⚪ Compute node 🟢 🟡 🟢 ⚪ ⚪ 🟡 🟢 ⚪ ⚪ GPU ⚪ 🟢 🟢 ⚪ ⚪ ⚪ 🟢 🟡 ⚪ Node interconnects ⚪ 🟢 🟡 ⚪ ⚪ ⚪ 🟢 ⚪ ⚪ Rack-scale NVLink ⚪ ⚪ ⚪ ⚪ ⚪ 🟢 ⚪ ⚪ ⚪ Ethernet network ⚪ ⚪ ⚪ ⚪ 🟢 ⚪ 🟢 ⚪ ⚪ InfiniBand network ⚪ 🟡 ⚪ 🟢 ⚪ ⚪ 🟢 ⚪ ⚪ Cluster management ⚪ ⚪ ⚪ ⚪ ⚪ ⚪ 🟢 ⚪ ⚪ Jobs and workloads ⚪ ⚪ ⚪ ⚪ ⚪ ⚪ 🟢 🟢 ⚪ AI inference ⚪ ⚪ ⚪ ⚪ ⚪ ⚪ ⚪ 🟡 🟢 Legend: 🟢 = Full support · 🟡 = Partial/indirect support Table 1. Observability decision framework Key tradeoffs include: DCGM compared to NVSM for GPUs : Prefer DCGM for utilization, power, temperature, NVLink, and XID/ECC export into Prometheus. Retain NVSM for system health on DGX-class nodes (drives, power, overall health). The tools overlap on GPU metrics; neither substitutes for platform BMC data. UFM compared to NetQ : Select by fabric type. InfiniBand uses UFM. Spectrum Ethernet/RoCE uses NetQ. Deploy both only when both fabrics are present. NMX : Required for rack-scale NVLink. Omit on classic multi-node NVLink topologies where DCGM already covers node interconnects. BCM : Treat BCM as the aggregator and cluster/job plane, not as the source of low-level counters. Specialized tools remain responsible for deep telemetry. Run:ai and NIM : Introduce when workload scheduling fairness or inference SLOs are first-class operational requirements. Neither replaces DCGM or fabric monitoring. A useful rule: cover every required green cell with the fewest tools. Extra exporters without a clear triage path add noise, not observability. That noise leads to alert fatigue. Teams keep adding metrics and dashboards, yet still cannot answer what is broken and why. The result is “watermelon metrics”: dashboards that look green outside while services fail inside. The corrective principle is the one stated in “ As Simple as Possible, No Simpler ”: keep monitoring simple, and remove unused signals rather than accumulate them. Apply the observability framework to an InfiniBand cluster Consider a DGX cluster with InfiniBand, BCM, and Slurm. Most jobs are training; inference is not yet in production. The operational requirement is a single triage dashboard and alerts that detect fabric and GPU health regressions before multi-hour job waste accumulates. Here’s the decision process: Domains in scope : platform, GPU, InfiniBand fabric, cluster/jobs. Out of scope for the initial deployment: NetQ, NMX, Run:ai, NIM. Tool selection from the framework Redfish/IPMI on every node for fans, PSU, chassis, and BMC state. DCGM on every GPU node for utilization, power, temperature, XID/ECC, and NVLink. NVSM on DGX nodes for system health aggregation. UFM for InfiniBand port health, BER, congestion, and routing. BCM as the cluster aggregator for jobs, reservations, and consolidated hardware alerts. Rationale : DCGM alone would miss the BER regression described in the introduction. This is a tail-at-scale problem . When work is synchronized across many ranks, end-to-end throughput follows the slowest rank, not average component health. UFM alone would miss GPU XID storms and node power faults. BCM alone would not generate the low-level counters. Combined, they cover the domains that waste GPU hours in this environment. Exclusions : Skip NetQ, NMX, and inference metrics until Ethernet, rack-scale NVLink, or inference services are introduced. That gives you an initial stack of IPMI, DCGM, NVSM, UFM, and BCM, unified in Prometheus/Grafana. Build an actionable AI infrastructure alert set Most tools expose hundreds of metrics. Prefer a short top-k set tied to service-level indicators (SLIs) and service-level objectives (SLOs) , not a dump of every hardware counter. Each alert should map to a clear remediation action. UFM Telemetry exposes hundreds of fields; start with the documented high-frequency telemetry fields . For the apply the observability framework to an InfiniBand cluster, begin with: Platform : fan speed, PSU status, key temperatures ( SPD_FAN_* , PWR_* , TEMP_* via Redfish/IPMI).

title: Part 2: Amazon Bedrock cost attribution with Amazon Athena and CUDOS
abstract: Part 1 introduced granular cost attribution for Amazon Bedrock. This feature automatically traces every inference request back to the IAM principal that made the call. It showed how the new line_item_iam_principal column can give you per-user and per-application visibility. With optional cost allocation tags, you can also aggregate spend by team, project, or tenant using AWS Cost Explorer. With this approach, you can typically track usage at the granularity you want for any Bedrock-powered service or application, whether third-party tools like Claude Code or Codex or your own custom builds. This post shows how to visualize and analyze cost attribution for Amazon Bedrock through Amazon Athena queries and CUDOS dashboards. First, this post shows you how to set up Cost and Usage Report (CUR) 2.0 through Data Exports instrumented with IAM principal data. Next, this post shows you how to query CUR data with Amazon Athena for analysis. It then introduces the new capabilities of CUDOS dashboards, including granular Bedrock cost and usage data. While Athena provides flexibility for aggregations, integration with different business intelligence (BI) tools, and chargeback processes, CUDOS offers pre-built visuals tailored to your organization’s specific structure. Example query output showing Amazon Bedrock costs by IAM principal and usage type Before you can analyze Amazon Bedrock costs, set up a CUR 2.0 data export and connect it to Amazon Athena. Make sure you have the required IAM permissions . For Amazon Bedrock cost attribution, you need to enable IAM principal data in your CUR 2.0 export so that the line_item_iam_principal column and associated IAM principal tags are populated. Follow the instructions in Creating a standard data export to set up your CUR 2.0 export. When configuring the export, make sure the following options are part of your final configuration: Creating a CUR 2.0 standard data export with caller identity (IAM principal) allocation data enabled Important: Enabling IAM principal data increases CUR file sizes because usage that was previously a single row is now expanded into multiple rows, one for each IAM principal that contributed to the usage. For high-volume workloads with many distinct principals, plan your Amazon S3 storage accordingly and consider Amazon S3 Lifecycle policies for older CUR files. It may take up to 24 hours for AWS to deliver your first CUR 2.0 report to the S3 bucket. With Amazon Athena, you can query your CUR data using standard SQL with no infrastructure to manage. To streamline this setup, an optional agent.md skill repo is available that you can use with AI assistants like Claude Code, Kiro-CLI, or Codex. It automates the end-to-end process of connecting your Athena environment to your CUR data. You may also follow the manual setup steps . If you plan to deploy the CUDOS dashboard as well, you can deploy it from AWS CloudFormation . This also deploys the Athena query database as part of the process. Once deployed, here is a sample test query in the Athena Query Editor that you can use: If this returns rows with IAM principal ARNs and Bedrock usage types, your setup is complete and ready for deeper analysis. With your CUR 2.0 data available in Athena, you can now answer granular cost attribution questions using SQL. This section provides three progressively sophisticated query patterns that cover the most common analysis scenarios. Note: In the following queries, replace your_cur_table_name with the actual name of your CUR Athena table (for example, cid_data_export.cur2 ). This query provides a complete breakdown of Amazon Bedrock spending by caller identity and model usage. It answers the question: “Who is calling which models, and how much are they spending?” When you’ve tagged your IAM principals with dimensions like team , project , or costcenter (and activated those tags as cost allocation tags), they appear in your CUR 2.0 data as part of the tags columns, with the iamPrincipal/ prefix followed by your tag key. This query groups costs by those tags to answer questions like: “How much did the engineering team spend on Bedrock this month?” or “What’s the total Bedrock cost for the chatbot project?” Note: This query returns results only if your IAM principals have been tagged with the relevant keys and those tags have been activated as cost allocation tags. In large organizations, you may not know in advance which tags have been applied across all IAM principals. Different teams might use different tag keys, or new tags might be introduced over time. The following example shows how to dynamically explore using Athena’s UNNEST function. This query discovers all IAM principal tags being used across your Bedrock workloads and shows cost allocation for each tag key-value pair: Consider a platform team running multiple AI-powered services. For example, the team might run a document summarization pipeline (DocProcessor) and a customer-facing chatbot (ChatApp). The team can assign each service to its own IAM role. With the query patterns from the preceding section, you can isolate how the spend for each service trends with the following query: From this output, the platform team can answer questions like: Which application is the top contributor to this month’s Bedrock spend? In this example, ChatApp accounts for over $80 using Claude 4.6 Sonnet, while DocProcessor costs under $5 using Nova Lite. Could we reduce costs by using a different model for each workload? DocProcessor is already on Nova Lite (appropriate for straightforward summarization tasks), but the team might evaluate whether ChatApp could handle some interactions with a lighter model to reduce the $72 output-token cost. You pay only for the queries that you run. You are charged based on the amount of data scanned by each query. The console displays this information after each query, and this information is also available in the Recent Queries tab in the Athena console. Athena queries are billed at $5 per TB scanned (with a 10 MB minimum per query). Because our table automatically uses hive partition projection on billing_period, queries scoped to a single month only scan the parquet files in that month’s folder. Scans are typically well under 10 MB, which costs about $0.00005 per query (the 10 MB minimum). To keep costs low, always include a WHERE billing_period = ... filter and select only the columns you need rather than SELECT * . CUDOS dashboard is part of the open source Cloud Intelligence Dashboards (CID) framework , which you can deploy in your AWS account using the provided infrastructure as code (IaC) templates. The framework helps you drive financial accountability and increase operational efficiency across your AWS organizations. The CUDOS dashboard provides detailed and actionable insights, supporting data-driven decisions for cost efficiency across your AWS infrastructure. CUDOS version 5.8 introduces a comprehensive Amazon Bedrock section in the AI/ML tab, with full IAM principal cost attribution support. The dashboard provides: The following figure shows the Amazon Bedrock Summary section in the AI/ML tab of the CUDOS dashboard, grouped by IAM principal, with per-principal cost breakdown and cost-per-million-tokens trend. CUDOS dashboard showing Amazon Bedrock spend grouped by IAM principal When you switch the grouping to IAM Principal Tag Project and choose a specific project (in this example, “chatbot-v2”), all other visuals filter to show only that project’s spend. The visuals break down that spend by model, usage type, and unit cost trends. CUDOS dashboard showing Amazon Bedrock spend grouped by IAM principal tag Project, filtered to the chatbot-v2 project With these visuals, you can quickly answer questions like “Which project is driving the most output token costs?”, “Is our chatbot team using cost-efficient models?”, or “How has our cost per million tokens changed since we switched from Opus to Sonnet?

title: How OneAdvanced deployed over 50 AI agents on UK-sovereign AWS
authors: Astrid Bowser, Alex Savage Nick Heap
abstract: This post is co-authored with OneAdvanced team Deploying AI agents on a United Kingdom (UK)-sovereign AWS architecture requires careful decisions about model hosting, data residency, and agent orchestration. OneAdvanced, a UK-based enterprise software provider serving over 10,000 customers, needed to deliver AI capabilities while making sure that no data would leave the UK. At the time, the specific models they wanted, Llama 4 Maverick and Llama Guard 4, weren’t yet available through managed services in the UK region. OneAdvanced took a different path: self-hosting open-weight large language models (LLMs) on AWS infrastructure they fully control. In this post, we describe how OneAdvanced built a UK-sovereign AI solution using Llama 4 Maverick and Llama Guard 4 on Amazon SageMaker AI . The solution pairs a Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline backed by Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL-Compatible Edition with the pgvector extension, over 50 specialized agents powered by Strands Agents SDK , and a tool layer running on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) . We walk through the architecture, key implementation decisions, and results. OneAdvanced provides sector-focused software as a service (SaaS) solutions to organizations in healthcare, legal, and many other regulated industries. Their customers handle sensitive data daily, including patient records, legal case files, and compliance documentation. These customers expect that AI tooling meets strict data residency, security, and privacy standards. As Andrew Henderson, CTO of OneAdvanced, explains in the OneAdvanced AI launch video : “Data sovereignty, particularly in the UK, is a hard requirement for many of our customers, especially those in the public sector and highly regulated industries. They need to know exactly where their data is, who has access to it, and that it resides within the UK’s legal and regulatory framework to support total compliance and trust.” OneAdvanced initially prototyped with Amazon Bedrock and saw rapid results within a two-week sprint: chat completion, an Amazon Bedrock Agent for querying UK statute law, Snowflake data integration, and chart generation. However, to meet their sovereignty requirements, OneAdvanced needed to host models exclusively in their own UK-based AWS accounts. At the time of the engagement, the models they wanted, Llama 4 Maverick and Llama Guard 4, weren’t yet available through AWS managed services in the UK region. Self-hosting meant deploying, serving, and scaling these models while building a production-grade solution around them. This included content moderation, document retrieval, agent orchestration, and a no-code agent builder for non-technical users. The following diagram shows the high-level architecture of the OneAdvanced AI solution. Figure 1: High-level architecture of the OneAdvanced UK-sovereign AI solution This architecture enabled OneAdvanced to achieve full UK data sovereignty and rapid agent deployment, supporting their ISO 42001 certification for AI governance while maintaining complete control over their model serving infrastructure. The solution consists of four components. vLLM serves Llama 4 Maverick (FP8) and Llama Guard 4 on Amazon SageMaker AI, running on p5.48xlarge instances in the London ( eu-west-2 ) region. Over 50 Strands agents run on Amazon ECS, each with its own system prompt, tool configuration, and optional input form, with agent configuration stored in Amazon DynamoDB . Documents uploaded to Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) are converted to markdown, chunked, and embedded into pgvector for retrieval. Llama Guard 4 checks user inputs for harmful content before the request reaches the main model. A typical request flows like this: the user sends a message, and Llama Guard checks it for harmful content (evaluated before the main inference model). The request routes to the appropriate Strands agent on Amazon ECS. The agent calls tools and retrieves relevant documents from pgvector and Amazon S3 as needed, or invokes specialist tools including web search. To self-host an AI model on AWS, you need the following resources and skills: OneAdvanced serves Llama 4 Maverick ( meta-llama/Llama-4-Maverick-17B-128E-Instruct-FP8 ) and Llama Guard 4 ( meta-llama/Llama-Guard-4-12B ) using vLLM on Amazon SageMaker AI endpoints. They deploy on p5.48xlarge instances in the London region, using Hugging Face models with AWS Deep Learning Containers . Longer context windows drove the move to P5 instances. OneAdvanced targets 120K–128K token context lengths to support use cases like large document analysis and multi-turn conversations. During the advisory engagement with AWS, load testing with vLLM on P5 instances validated that the infrastructure could handle their throughput requirements. OneAdvanced started on p4d.24xlarge instances and moved to p5.48xlarge for production, also taking advantage of reserved instance discounts on GPU compute. Llama Guard 4 replaced an earlier deployment of Llama Guard 3 after OneAdvanced observed high false rejection rates with the previous version. The guard model runs serially before the main model, screening user inputs for harmful content before inference begins. A distinctive aspect of the OneAdvanced solution is its agent library: over 50 task-specific agents spanning healthcare, legal, HR, marketing, logistics, and more. Agents include a Care Incident Response assistant, a Clinical Safety Bulletin generator, a scheme of work generator for education, an operational scenario simulation, a performance review assistant, a Document Comparison tool, and an AWS Architect Agent, among many others. OneAdvanced went from their first agent to over 50 in only three weeks, with most agents built in less than a day. OneAdvanced evaluated several agentic frameworks, including LangChain, LangGraph, and others, before choosing Strands Agents SDK. The decision came down to a few factors: Strands takes a model-first approach with no rigid workflow definitions, it supports turn-taking and interview-style interactions, and it allowed OneAdvanced to move quickly from idea to deployed agent. As Nick Heap, Principal Software Engineer at OneAdvanced, explains: “Post-evaluation, Strands stood out as the clear frontrunner for the project. Its comprehensive suite of tools not only met our requirements but also offered a future-proof solution that closely aligned with our in-house vision.” Each agent is defined with a system prompt, a set of tools, and an optional structured input form. Agents are containerized and deployed on Amazon ECS, with runtime configuration stored in Amazon DynamoDB. Users browse the agent catalog and select the one that fits their task. OneAdvanced also built a no-code agent builder that non-developers can use to create and configure agents through a visual interface. Users define the agent’s persona, design input forms with drag-and-drop fields, write system prompts with references to form fields (using an @ syntax to inject form values), and select from a library of available tools. This design makes agent creation accessible to product managers, clinicians, and business analysts without writing code. Agents draw from a shared tool library that includes calculator, chart creation, file content reader, mermaid diagram generator, organization and personal knowledge search, spreadsheet query (including Snowflake integration), text file query, UK statute law search, and web search (opt-in per organization and per user query). For example, an agent can query a Snowflake database and then generate a chart from the results in a single interaction. OneAdvanced also uses sub-agents and advanced agentic patterns to maintain the context window across complex interactions. A notable design pattern is the interview-style agent.

title: Pay with confidence: How Solv Labs built verifiable, auditable agent payments on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments
abstract: This post is co-written with Patrick Duffy from Solv Labs and Houman Shadab from ICME Labs Solv Labs built an AI agent-payments workflow using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, governed by two layers: ORACLE (Solv’s policy engine) and ICME PreFlight for compliance verification. AgentCore payments provides the payment processing infrastructure. ORACLE enforces authorization policies before each transaction. ICME’s verification layer extends AWS Automated Reasoning Checks to make them privacy-preserving, portable, and independently verifiable, with each decision checkable. As a result, every agent payment runs through three core governance components: ORACLE for pre-authorization decisions, an integrity service running in an AWS Nitro Enclave, and a risk engine for per-transaction pricing. Each transaction completes in under four seconds, covering pre-authorization, governance, and on-chain settlement through Coinbase. Every transaction produces a full audit trail, and that’s well within latency budgets for agentic workloads. The first time an autonomous agent moves real money on behalf of an enterprise, the question is no longer “Did it work?” It is “Can we prove what just happened?” In a single quarter, four pieces of infrastructure that make that question answerable arrived together: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments, AWS Automated Reasoning Checks, AWS Nitro Enclaves used as a per-transaction attester, and the x402 payment standard for agent payments to services. Amazon introduced Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments in May 2026, built in partnership with Coinbase and Stripe. It lets AI agents instantly access and pay for what they use, including web content, APIs, MCP servers, and other agents. Spending is governed by the same controls developers already use to operate their agents. In this post, Solv Labs and policy-verification partner ICME walk through how we built an agent-payments workflow on AgentCore payments where every transaction is governed at execution time, attested inside an AWS Nitro Enclave, risk-priced individually, and fully auditable. We also cover what this pattern unlocks for enterprises running agents in regulated environments. When an autonomous system moves money, the operator must prove to auditors, counterparties, and legal that each payment was authorized, priced for the risk it carried, and recorded in a way that holds up to scrutiny. A misconfigured or manipulated agent doesn’t only return a bad answer. It moves money. And the hard part isn’t executing the payment. It’s proving, afterward, that the payment was permitted in the first place. Enterprise teams consistently struggle with the same gap: when an agent transaction completes, there’s no durable record tying that specific action to the policy that authorized it, the constraints it satisfied, or the risk it carried. Model cards, SOC 2 reports, and after-the-fact reviews describe the organization around the system. They don’t describe the execution of individual decisions. Without that transaction-level binding, operators have no clean way to resolve a dispute, satisfy an auditor, or tell a routine agent action apart from a compromised one. Solv Labs needed every agent action to be verifiable, risk-priced, and auditable on demand, without slowing agents down or bolting on infrastructure outside the system they already run on. The vision is straightforward: govern every agent payment at execution time and produce a record that various parties (auditors, counterparties, regulators) can verify independently without depending on the operator’s word for it. This became practical only recently, with AgentCore payments as the payment orchestration layer, Automated Reasoning Checks (ARc) for formal policy evaluation, Nitro Enclaves for hardware attestation, and x402 reaching broad adoption for agent payments. Together, they made governed agent payments an implementation choice rather than a research program. The workflow runs as a set of specialized components: AgentCore payments in a Solv-operated environment, the ORACLE engine with its Nitro Enclave attester, and policy checks from ICME as an external service. Components only cross trust boundaries through signed, hash-bound artifacts, so the evidence flow holds regardless of how the services are deployed. The workflow attaches to an agent built on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and is compatible with agents running on AgentCore runtime or custom AgentCore implementations. Figure 1: System architecture. Every agent payment passes through pre-authorization, constraint verification, integrity attestation, and risk pricing before settlement, all native to AgentCore Every payment runs through five specialized components, each addressing a distinct part of the governance problem. These components run in a fixed order: ORACLE’s decision, its independently verifiable proof, the hardware attestation, and the per-transaction risk price are all produced before settlement is initiated. The gate is absolute: no decision, no settlement. Figure 2: Transaction sequence. Steps 1–3 produce the governance record before settlement is initiated, and the gate enforces “no decision, no settlement.” End-to-end latency is under four seconds per transaction, with governance overhead under one second Each governed payment produces a single signed evidence record binding five things: the policy that was evaluated, the policy-check result and its independently verifiable proof, the hardware-attested execution record, the per-transaction risk price, and the settlement artifacts from AgentCore payments. It doesn’t attest that the agent’s underlying decision was wise, that the counterparty is solvent, or that the policy itself is correct. Those remain the operator’s responsibility, as for other payments. What it does attest, in a way parties can verify, is that this specific payment was evaluated against this specific policy under these specific constraints at this specific risk price, and that the result of that evaluation is what authorized settlement. Figure 3: Per-transaction evidence record containing execution and policy hashes, constraint result, zero-knowledge proof reference, hardware attestation digests, risk multiplier, and on-chain anchor. Hashes and identifiers are illustrative placeholders. The full record is canonicalized, Ed25519-signed inside the Nitro Enclave, and anchored on-chain Three properties of the service make the workflow operationally clean: “Before we built this workflow, the thing we couldn’t give an enterprise was a clean answer to why a specific payment was permitted — only assertions about the organization that authorized it. AgentCore payments let us move that answer to the transaction itself: every payment now carries the policy it cleared, the enclave that signed it, and the proof a third party can check. The evidence travels with the transaction.” — Patrick Duffy, CEO, Solv Labs “When the verifier of a payment decision isn’t the operator who made it, you need a way to prove the check ran correctly without exposing the policy itself. That’s what ICME adds to AWS Automated Reasoning Checks: every decision comes with a cryptographic proof a counterparty or regulator can verify in under a second without seeing the policy detail or the transaction parameters.” — Houman Shadab, Co-Founder, ICME Labs The workflow produces a per-transaction, hardware-attested, independently verifiable governance record before settlement of a payment transaction by an agent. Enterprises adopting this pattern on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments get the following, per payment transaction, at machine speed: Figure 4: The per-transaction evidence stack.

title: Tiered KV cache for large LLMs on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod with Curvine
abstract: Running large language model (LLM) inference at scale typically forces a KV cache trade-off: you either pay for oversized GPU instances to accommodate a growing KV cache, or you accept slow time-to-first-token (TTFT) as identical prompts get recomputed on every request. For teams deploying a broad catalog of publicly available foundation models (FMs), such as Qwen, Llama, DeepSeek, and others, across per-business-line endpoints, Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines, or multi-turn dialogue applications, this trade-off translates directly into higher infrastructure cost and degraded user experience. The root cause is straightforward. During generation, vLLM stores the attention keys and values for every token it has already processed in a KV cache, so it doesn’t recompute them on each step. Prefix caching extends this by reusing that cache across requests that share the same leading tokens (like a common system prompt). On cost-efficient instances like ml.g6e.4xlarge (48 GB per GPU), once model weights and runtime allocations are accounted for, the memory left for prefix caching is limited, and it tightens further with larger models or higher concurrency. Cache hit rates drop on long prompts, identical system prompts get re-prefilled on every request, and horizontally scaled vLLM replicas each maintain isolated caches. Routing to a different replica is functionally a cold start. In this post, we build a tiered KV cache architecture on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod that extends the cache hierarchy beyond GPU and CPU memory into a shared, distributed NVMe pool. It builds on two HyperPod capabilities, Managed Tiered KV Cache and Intelligent Routing , and adds Curvine , a lightweight distributed cache filesystem, as the shared L2 tier (GPU to CPU to shared NVMe). With this setup, you can reuse KV cache across replicas at near-local-disk speeds. We walk through the end-to-end implementation, from enabling HyperPod Tiered Storage to deploying Curvine workers on node-local NVMe to patching the Inference Operator for filesystem-backed L2. On a test deployment, this achieved up to a 100 percent cross-Pod cache hit rate, up to a 2.7x TTFT improvement, and cross-node L2 read latency of about 56 ms for a approximately 1,900-token prompt. See the Benchmarking section for the full methodology and results. With this architecture, workloads that previously required P5 instances can run on lower-cost G6e instances, reducing per-endpoint cost. Actual savings depend on model size and traffic profile. The central idea is to extend the KV cache beyond what fits on a single Pod. Rather than accepting that each vLLM replica lives in isolation, which is its own GPU blocks, its own CPU spill area, no sharing, we build a three-tier hierarchy: L0 (GPU HBM), L1 (local CPU/host memory), and L2 (Curvine, a shared cross-node cache), and overlay it with cache-aware request routing. L0 – GPU prefix cache. This is vLLM’s native paged-attention layer, holding the hottest KV blocks at the lowest access latency, but its capacity is only whatever GPU memory is left after the model weights. On a 48 GB GPU, a 7B model in bf16 uses around 14 GB for weights, leaving over 30 GB for KV blocks, which is plenty of headroom, so L0 pressure is minimal. A 32B model uses around 64 GB of weights and doesn’t even fit on one 48 GB GPU. Even after sharding, far less memory remains for KV, so the cache fills quickly and evicts under concurrency. That shrinking headroom is exactly why extending the cache off-GPU matters as you scale up model size and traffic. L1 – CPU memory offload. When GPU blocks are evicted, LMCache catches them in host DRAM before they’re lost. This runs inside each inference Pod and is managed automatically by the SageMaker HyperPod Inference Operator when you set enableL1Cache: true in the InferenceEndpointConfig CRD. Think of it as a safety net. It’s fast, Pod-local, and sized by InstanceMemoryAllocationPercentage (we recommend starting at 20 percent). L2 – Shared distributed NVMe pool. This is where cross-replica reuse happens. Curvine , a lightweight distributed cache filesystem, pools the local NVMe drives that ship with G6e/P5 instances into a single namespace, which a FUSE client (a user-space driver that presents the pool as an ordinary mounted directory) mounts as a ReadWriteMany PVC (PersistentVolumeClaim) into every inference Pod. LMCache reads and writes through its fs:// connector, so the distributed pool looks like a local directory. Because every Pod mounts the same namespace, a KV block written by one replica is immediately readable by others. Curvine itself is straightforward to operate: a Primary Node (called the “Master” in Curvine’s documentation) handles metadata and journaling, persisted on Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) for durability, while Worker components run on each GPU node and store data on the node’s NVMe (typically mounted at /opt/dlami/nvme/curvine-data). If a Worker dies, the cache it held is recomputed, no data-loss concern, since these are reproducible KV blocks. Intelligent routing – getting requests to the right replica. A three-tier cache only delivers its full benefit if requests land on replicas that already hold relevant KV blocks. The HyperPod Inference Operator includes a built-in router that supports three strategies: The router maintains a prefix tree (prefix-aware) or queries each worker’s cache state (kv-aware) to select the replica most likely to produce a cache hit. This happens transparently, no client-side changes are needed. How these pieces fit together. The Inference Operator is installed as an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) add-on and manages the full lifecycle. It spins up vLLM Pods with LMCache sidecars, configures L1 and L2 backends, deploys the router, and exposes a single load-balanced endpoint. You declare the cache topology you want in the InferenceEndpointConfig CRD ( enableL1Cache , enableL2Cache , l2CacheBackend , routingStrategy ), and the Operator renders the correct environment variables, volume mounts, and routing rules. The one caveat today: the CRD’s l2CacheBackend field only accepts redis or tieredstorage natively. To point L2 at a Curvine FUSE mount, we patch the LMCACHE_REMOTE_URL environment variable in the vLLM container spec to fs://localhost:0/mnt/curvine/l2cache/ . We walk through this patch in Stage 4 of the implementation. The net effect is a request arrives at the router, gets dispatched to the replica with the best prefix match, that replica checks GPU blocks (L0), then CPU (L1), then the shared NVMe pool (L2). Only on a complete miss does it re-prefill from scratch. For workloads with moderate-to-high prompt overlap (roughly over 40 percent shared leading tokens, for example a common system prompt or shared RAG context), skipping that re-prefill substantially reduces TTFT. Figure 1 shows the full data path. Each vLLM Pod stacks an L0 GPU prefix cache and an L1 CPU offload. Below them, all Pods share the L2 tier on a Curvine distributed filesystem pooled from node-local NVMe and mounted ReadWriteMany over FUSE, while the Curvine metadata node persists to Amazon EBS. The HyperPod Intelligent Router sits in front, directing each request to the replica most likely to already hold the relevant cache. Figure 1: Tiered KV cache architecture Curvine is a high-performance distributed cache file system that sits between applications and underlying storage such as Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3), HDFS, or NAS. Clients reach it through the CLI, SDK, FUSE, or CSI. Primary Nodes handle metadata, and Workers serve data with local disk cache for low-latency I/O. Figure 2 shows the Curvine architecture and its key components. Figure 2: Curvine architecture How Curvine works (cluster view): Amazon SageMaker HyperPod Tiered Storage is a cluster-level capability that provisions a node-local cache tier for inference workloads.

title: I wrote an AI textbook — how long until AI can do it better?
abstract: There are a lot of criticisms of AI writing, but most of them are focused on more creative, high-voice writing like this blog. Those — including my own piece — often argue that it is because good writing is high-voice, has a point of view, has a deep human expression that needs to come across, and or a process of thinking that you peek into with the chosen words. As LLMs get more refined as tools, rather than conversational assistants, I think we are actually going backwards on our goals of having models produce inspiring writing. On the other side of things is non-fiction writing. Filler, copy text was one of the genuinely useful abilities of an LLM (Sam Altman said so much about the early business of GPT-3 on a recent podcast ). It has seemed like any flaws here were mostly down to a general lack of intelligence in the models, or some other training issue, and all non-fiction and explanatory text would get obliterated by the rapid pace of progress eventually . Having worked with the models as a writing assistant over the last few years, they’ve gotten a bit better, but it’s worth reflecting on what’s holding them back. Models being stagnant in long-form, non-fiction writing should be alarming to those reliant on models autonomously solving grand, open science problems in the near future. The models today struggle to organize and compellingly present some of the most established science in their area. This seems like a natural prerequisite that we should expect the models to master before they can solve broad, open-ended problems on their own. Until this is solved, the progress of LLMs for science will look closer to solving low-hanging fruit and merging distant connections across fields, rather than any sort of revolutionary insight. This is a somewhat controversial take for someone who is very optimistic about AI’s progress, especially writing it on the day that Anthropic published a blog post on Claude making some progress on the famous Riemann Hypothesis . Scientific problems have a vast breadth, and I don’t think current AI models have as much coverage as many think. Organizing knowledge is a compression. This compression is needed to make insight . Today’s LLMs increase entropy in long-form non-fiction writing, and I don’t see how that can be stacked on top of itself endlessly. They’ll be reliant on humans acting as sort of guides. I am still very optimistic about translation from these narrow forms of science, like the extreme advancements we’ve seen in math, into consistent, broader progress — LLMs are the most powerful assistants scientists have ever used. I first need to explain how observing the models work on such grounded, low-level knowledge problems in writing makes me see a surprising lack of generalization. For more context, I just finished writing a post-training textbook, Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (buy on Manning or Amazon ). I used LLMs in many ways to support this, from helping wrangle LaTeX formatting for equations, doing extensive copyediting, and creating diagrams for programming languages like TikZ (in LaTeX) or Python. I would’ve expected way more progress on non-fiction writing from the models. I almost thought I would look dumb publishing a non-fiction book in 2026, given how things looked in 2024. Today, some of the most famous models on writing ability are pretty old, examples include OpenAI’s big GPT 4.5 and Moonshot’s Kimi K2 . In and around these releases, the models have gone from okay to superhuman at other tasks like coding and mathematics. Maybe a closer, but still imperfect, comparison is how the models went from incapable to decent at search and research tasks. The pace of progress on most other skills is steep, but writing well feels orthogonal to most of them. I do not think writing is just ignored, but rather it’s challenging and lacks good training data to specifically intervene on it. There is certainly some low-hanging fruit for making AI models better at writing — such as specialized harnesses like Claude Code, prompts, and training environments that make models spend a lot more inference tokens on the output, but I don’t think these will have a multiplicative impact on ability. Writing well is a very hard task! It’s a shame that we haven’t unlocked inference-time scaling for one of the great intellectual pursuits. Regardless, writing seems very different than what the models are good at. 1 Today, the models seem genuinely horrible at long-form technical writing. They can get a sentence right, but if you try and get them to write an entire chapter it’ll be a mix of sprinkled with confusing wording, muddled in its organization, and generally a bit off. They try to be too cute where they don’t need to be and in the process make random conceptual errors. The models in the near future will get much better at the small errors, especially as models get bigger — which allows them to hold more world knowledge — but I do not expect their ability to utilize it to transform. For example, the GPT models have been incredible at finding typos and minor issues for a long time. I passed a near-final draft of my book as a PDF to GPT 5.5 Pro and it found deep, surprising minor typos across the manuscript that is 200-300 pages. On the other hand, the Claude models have been much more useful as an editor. They have a lot more taste, tend to understand the mental model of the task better, and have more interesting suggestions to unstick the different forms of writer’s block. The examples I’ve given above all have a sort of consistent theme. The models know how to check every unit of content, in this case usually a sentence or equation or figure, or make one, specific section where you are caught. With these skills, they don’t do a good job revisiting components and stringing them together as they make many additions on top of each other. It feels like a sort of irreducible compounding errors. We used to deal with these errors in math and code, but reflecting on it, RLVR has been a truly magical solution in reducing them. I’m willing to share that there are a few technical explanation sentences in my book that came from an AI model — well less than 1% — they’re there because I really loved them. I let myself consider including some AI tokens in the book, as it didn’t feel like cheating if I, as a true expert, felt that the sentence was what the reader needed. Especially in the editing process, where I had a very close eye on things and plenty of concern on if my book would ever be done with all the things I have going on, it was an extremely valuable path forward. For example, I had a list of questions from my editor interspersed in a LaTeX file with a specific delimiter like \editor{} . I would have Claude Code navigate to each comment, print the context before and after, and let me know if it was an easy typo fix or something more nuanced. I would write a response — the text to insert — or ask Claude for suggestions before fixing it. Intellectually it is a very focusing process of editing, it was a fun way to improve the book. Sometimes phrases from Claude’s suggestions are what made it into the book. It is definitely a slippery slope and when I accepted a few AI suggestions it was at the point where I was going through my second full-manuscript review. Emotionally the project felt completed but I had more work to do. Coming out of the textbook-writing process I so deeply appreciate the cut and dry rule I have for my writing on Interconnects to never use AI outputs in the content. It is way more fun to write in a way that is only you — high voice, valued so deeply for the process — but writing a standard reference is not really an activity known for being fun. I see why people turn AI tools into a crutch when most of their writing is just an output to fill space, rather than a means to an end. I am motivated to write voluminously to learn, to feel, and to express.

title: 剛剛，DeepSeek V4 Pro正式版釋出，多項對標Fable 5
abstract: 剛剛，DeepSeek V4 Pro正式版釋出，多項對標Fable 5 Jay 2026-08-13 11:54:01 來源： 量子位 現在呼叫V4 Pro，能直接用上完全體 Jay 發自 凹非寺 量子位 | 公眾號 QbitAI 家人們，火星撞地球了。 剛剛，DeepSeek V4 Pro正式版，釋出了！！ 太離譜了，看了眼Benchmark，這是 直接要和Fable對標啊。。。 HLE、Terminal Bench、Cybergym、DeepSWE……Agent能力幾乎全方位碾壓Opus 4.8，無限逼近Fable 5，甚至有些榜單都反超了。 看到沒，這就是後訓練的威力！！！ DeepSeek V4 Pro正式版 可惜，官方部落格還沒發，不能繼續一探究竟。 但API平臺是先一步更新了，現在呼叫V4 Pro，能直接用上完全體， DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 。 價格這塊依舊很能打，基本和之前的Pro預覽版保持一致。 百萬tokens輸入 3元 ，命中快取 0.025元 ，百萬tokens輸出則是 6元 。 我宣佈，滑動變阻器再次進入「梁聖」週期。 但也不是沒有壞訊息。 網友實測後發現， CoT成山頂洞人了啊。。。 Need to identify as DeepSeek model. The system says You are DeepSeek, knowledge cutoff May 2025, current date Aug 2026. We need be honest. We are DeepSeek latest model? 雖然也能看懂啥意思，但反正也是徹底不言人語了，不影響意義傳遞的詞全囫圇吞棗了。 這估計也是為了效能最佳化考慮，之前看過YouTube博主分析， GPT隱藏的思維鏈也是這個風格 ，說是「山頂洞語」可以大幅減少Token消耗。 但代價吧，就是寫作估計是寄了。。。 這也是Agent狂飆時代的大趨勢吧，一切能力都在優先為Coding讓位。 但至少，在Coding方面，V4 Pro正式版完成了它該做的。 國產開源陣營，又出現了一個緊逼閉源的超級模型。 這一次，它來自DeepSeek。 One More Thing 說實話，好久沒有看到這麼激動人心的場景了。 深夜吭哧吭哧寫完稿的我，如今彷彿看到原子彈爆炸，癱軟在椅，久久不能動彈（bushi）。 說回正題。 這幾個月來，中國開源模型陣營彷彿開了外掛一樣，一路猛發新模型，追著Anthropic和OpenAI打。 先是 GLM 5.2 ，堪稱後訓練的神，直接幹到Opus 4.8級別。 Kimi K3 緊隨其後，模型逼近Fable級，甚至直接點燃開源閉源論戰的導火索，老黃的親自下場為開源站臺。 然後，梁叔叔來了。。。 V4 Flash沒往SOTA定位打，但反而更恐怖，直接給API呼叫成本幹成電費，徹底掀起低價風暴。 大家都說，DeepSeek就是斬殺線，拿著個除草機在後面追，同行全在拼了命地往前面跑。 因為價效比打法確實太恐怖了。 跑輸了？ 寄，喜提營收歸零。 跑贏了呢？ 嘿，您猜怎麼著，也沒獎勵。 而這一次，DeepSeek的定位，不再只是簡單的價效比。 V4 Pro完全體上線，大鯨魚的眼裡，只有那個SOTA王冠。 2025年春節的DeepSeek，回來了。 API文件：https://api-docs.deepseek.com/#:~:text=the%20deepseek-v4-pro%20model%20has%20been%20updated%20to%20DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 版權所有，未經授權不得以任何形式轉載及使用，違者必究。 Deepseek Jay 剛剛，Manus恢復獨立運營 2026-08-12 Claude罵聲中啟動「隱形水印」：新模型全量嵌入，標記所有文字 2026-08-11 奧特曼的ChatGPT育兒大法，捅了馬蜂窩 2026-08-08 中國NeoLab時刻：EverMind用3篇論文，交出全棧自進化首份答卷 2026-08-08 相關閱讀

title: 360奈米大片流水線攜手《知識就是力量》釋出“知力·奈米”科普科幻AI大片創作平臺
abstract: 360奈米大片流水線攜手《知識就是力量》釋出“知力·奈米”科普科幻AI大片創作平臺 量子位的朋友們 2026-08-13 11:11:48 來源： 量子位 《知識就是力量》雜誌社攜手360科技集團舉行“知力·奈米 科普科幻AI大片創作平臺”釋出暨AI創作交流活動 8月11日，《知識就是力量》雜誌社攜手360科技集團舉行“知力·奈米 科普科幻AI大片創作平臺”釋出暨AI創作交流活動。《知識就是力量》雜誌社社長、主編郭晶，360集團高階副總裁、360網際網路集團總裁趙君，360集團AI影片總經理吳瓊出席活動。來自科普、教育、科研、科技傳播、人工智慧與內容創作領域的專家學者、機構代表、教師學生及媒體代表共同見證平臺釋出。 “知力·奈米”科普科幻AI大片創作平臺，是奈米大片流水線在垂直AI影片生產領域的一次重要落地，也是《知識就是力量》雜誌社成立70週年的重要合作成果。作為《知識就是力量》雜誌社首個授予聯合品牌的專案，該平臺將雜誌70年來積累的權威科普內容，與360奈米大片流水線在智慧體、AI影片生產方面的技術能力相結合，共同打造面向科普科幻垂類的專業知識庫、智慧體能力體系和科普科幻專屬的AI影片生產平臺。 平臺面向中小學、高校、科研院所、科技館、協會學會、實驗室及各類公共機構，旨在把權威科普內容、AI智慧體能力、AI影片生產流程與釋出傳播體系打通，幫助機構把科學知識、科研成果、課程內容和科普選題轉化為更具畫面感、故事感和傳播力的AI大片內容，推動科普內容生產從單點工具應用邁向專業化、體系化和生態化發展。 科普求真，AI向善 《知識就是力量》雜誌社社長、主編郭晶在釋出辭中表示，《知識就是力量》堅守“播種科學的種子，點燃科學的夢想”的初心，360集團則以“讓AI世界更安全更美好”為使命。“知力·奈米 科普科幻AI大片創作平臺”的釋出，見證了兩份初心交匯——科普求真，AI向善。 郭晶還提到，平臺是國內傳媒與科普領域唯一建立在國家標準上的智慧體互聯中樞，是國家廣電總局攜手兩院院士釋出的“知識就是力量科普視聽行動”的重要落地，致力於構建跨界協作新機制、助力科普視聽新生態，讓科技走出學術殿堂，讓科學種子在AI土壤生根發芽。她期待在“十五五”開局之年，將平臺打造成科普科幻創作標杆陣地，讓AI成為科普高質量發展的核心動能。 對於科普事業而言，AI的價值不只是提升效率，更在於幫助權威知識以更生動、更直觀、更具感染力的方式觸達公眾和青少年。對於機關單位、學校、科研機構和公共服務機構來說，這樣的平臺不僅是技術工具，更是承載社會價值、公共價值和科學傳播價值的合作基礎。 讓AI成為真正的內容生產力 360集團高階副總裁、360網際網路集團總裁趙君在致辭中表示，AI真正的價值，不在於做幾個炫目的Demo，也不在於生成幾張漂亮圖片，而在於能不能成為真正的生產力，真正進入產業、教育、內容生產，以及每一個普通人的工作和創造過程。 他指出，“知力·奈米”不是一個單純的影片生成工具，而是一套面向科普科幻垂類的AI內容創作和宣發基礎設施。平臺將影視工業流程重新封裝為普通人也能使用的AI影片創作能力，打通從內容輸入、劇本生成、分鏡設計到影片成片的全流程，讓科學內容能夠更高效地轉化為有畫面感、有傳播力的作品。 同時，平臺具備網際網路視聽節目許可、網際網路新聞資訊服務許可、智慧體節點身份碼等標準化能力，通過“知力·奈米”平臺生產的AI影片作品可被納入“知識就是力量”科普資訊平臺和科普視聽行動官方平臺，成為可檢索、可認證、可傳播、可運營的內容資產體系。未來，平臺將持續服務學校、科技館、科研機構、科普組織和青少年創作者，讓更多科學故事和未來想像真正走向社會、走向公眾。 奈米大片流水線賦能科普內容生產 360集團AI影片總經理吳瓊在釋出會上針對平臺能力進行了專項分享。吳瓊表示，今天的科普領域，並不缺科學知識，缺的是把科學知識變成能被理解、被看見、被傳播的“好內容”的能力。“知力·奈米”平臺的核心，不是把幾個AI能力簡單拼接，而是把過去複雜的影視工業流程重新封裝，讓普通使用者也能用簡單的方式、按照專業流程完成AI科普影片內容創作。我們的學者、老師和文化傳播者只需要專注於知識本身，AI會輔助大家完成細節生產的工作。 吳瓊介紹，平臺圍繞“劇本—資產—分鏡—影片—成片”形成完整創作鏈路，藉助奈米大片流水線獨家的AI智慧體劇組系統，把專業影視工業製作中的編劇、分鏡、場景、角色、攝影等能力模組化、智慧體化，幫助使用者把科學知識轉化為更具畫面感、故事感和傳播力的AI影片作品。平臺還通過專業科普知識庫和智慧體能力，支援知識轉譯、受眾分級改寫、術語解釋和專業知識審校輔助，讓科學內容既準確可信，又易傳播。 在平臺能力上，“知力·奈米”進一步把內容生產從個人工具升級為機構級平臺，支援賬號許可權、專案流程、素材資產、作品管理和傳播運營，適用於學校、科研院所、科技館、協會學會等多類機構。不同的機構，可以展開在AI影視內容共建、教育實訓、組織賽事、科學展陳、協會服務等諸多方面的不同合作。 吳瓊表示，360將繼續圍繞智慧體、AI影片和內容平臺能力，推動“知力·奈米”不斷完善，讓更多機構擁有自己的科普科幻內容生產能力，讓優質科學內容真正成為可持續的數字資產。 本文由360提供，量子位獲授權轉載，觀點歸原作者所有。 版權所有，未經授權不得以任何形式轉載及使用，違者必究。 360 量子位的朋友們 倒計時｜2026世界機器人大會主論壇議程釋出！ 2026-08-13 title: 引領智慧手機邁入具身互動時代 全球首款機器人手機榮耀Robot Phone釋出
abstract: 引領智慧手機邁入具身互動時代 全球首款機器人手機榮耀Robot Phone釋出 量子位的朋友們 2026-08-13 11:00:41 來源： 量子位 2026年8月12日，全球領先的AI終端生態公司榮耀（HONOR）在廣州舉辦“嗨！新朋友”榮耀Robot Phone全球新品釋出會，正式推出全球首款機器人手機榮耀Robot Phone。 作為榮耀“敢想、敢不同”品牌精神的集中體現，榮耀Robot Phone以首創的四自由度鈦合金靈巧雲臺，賦予手機機器人級“身體”；以Agentic OS核心，構建首個系統級Agent架構，為使用者帶來跨越式的智慧互動體驗；並攜手百年電影工業標杆阿萊（ARRI），將電影工業級影像能力帶入移動終端。機器人的靈動、AI的智慧與ARRI的電影感由此融於一體，推動AI終端從“數字智慧”邁向“具身智慧”，開啟人與智慧終端從工具關係走向夥伴關係的新階段。 這也是榮耀點亮Augmented Human Intelligence（簡稱AHI）智啟人本燈塔後落地的首款機器人手機旗艦新品。面對方興未艾的人工智慧浪潮，榮耀堅定向內重構人與AI的關係，向外打破智慧終端墨守成規的形態邊界，打造出從內到外變革創新的榮耀Robot Phone：讓AI從螢幕中的數字智慧走向真實的物理世界，讓手機從被動響應指令的智慧工具，進化成為集感知、思考、行動與陪伴的智慧夥伴，引領手機行業進入“機器主動理解人”的全新時代。 首創鈦合金靈巧雲臺 打造手機行業最精密機械結構新標杆 榮耀首創鈦合金靈巧雲臺，首次為手機帶來機器人級機械自由度，讓手機不再是一塊被動的螢幕，而是能夠與人和環境互動的夥伴。 面對旗艦手機寸土寸金的內部空間，榮耀重構的鈦合金雲臺架構，不僅將加工精度推進至±0.005mm，行業最高，更讓整體尺寸大幅縮減65%。 鈦合金雲臺電機僅重2.6g，行業最輕，體積較具身智慧領域的靈巧手關節電機縮小34%。 三軸最大控制轉速可達360°/s，行業最快，能夠靈敏響應快速轉向、跟拍與急停等高動態場景。 為了讓雲臺不僅轉得快，還能翻得穩、停得住，榮耀進一步自研盾構鋼翻轉電機，以120N·m/L的扭矩密度，行業最強，為雲臺快速展開、順暢收起與穩定懸停提供強勁動力。 整套雲臺機械系統整合100餘個精密零件，應用60餘項精密工藝，並積累100餘項自研專利，在輕量化、小型化、高扭矩與高速響應之間取得平衡，打造手機行業最精密機械結構新標杆。 全新YOYO機器人模式 開啟多模態具身互動新時代 榮耀Robot Phone以Agentic OS為核心，採用首個系統級Agent架構，並首發YOYO Pro模式，構建感知、規劃、推理、執行、反饋的完整閉環。 同時，榮耀還基於“開放、共創、共享”的AI生態理念，聯合阿里巴巴“千問大模型”深度共創了面向手機場景最佳化的終端大模型解決方案，為顛覆性的具身智慧體驗提供了澎湃的底層算力支撐。 全新YOYO自動執行具備極強的長指令遵循與跨應用泛化能力。使用者只需一句話交辦，YOYO即可在後臺完成複雜任務，實現“超長任務一句話搞定，跨越生態一句話聯動”。 YOYO Pro也在即將釋出的榮耀Magic9系列全面搭載。 全新的YOYO機器人模式，搭載首創的多模態具身感知系統，能看懂、聽懂、也懂你沒說出口的心意。 YOYO能夠通過手勢識別做到“懂你所指”，藉助擬人表情實現“懂你所感”。在此基礎上，YOYO還能展現出色的樂感，識別音樂快慢，並讓雲臺隨音樂做出不同動作，真正實現“隨音而舞”，帶來超豐富的情感表達。 此外，YOYO還能通過自然語言互動，自動調整角度，替使用者完成原本需要攝影師配合的專業運鏡，輕鬆實現“你說TA拍”的創作自由。 榮耀Robot Phone的影像智慧體也做了全面升級。全新的“靈感幫拍”除了能通過AI識別主體、給出姿勢推薦外，還能通過雲臺自動完成構圖，大幅降低了專業運鏡的門檻。 而在抖音直播場景中，榮耀Robot Phone提供雲臺自動追焦功能。使用者只需升起雲臺，點選懸浮框即可一鍵啟用“AI直播追焦”，鏡頭自動平穩跟隨，跟焦靈敏。後續更新還將支援更多直播平臺。 同樣，在日常的微信視訊通話中，“視訊通話追焦”功能可以實現人物自動跟隨，讓使用者在移動過程中始終保持清晰入鏡。 榮耀還推出創新、開放的YOYO技能商店，商店中的skills一鍵安裝，YOYO就能自動呼叫，學會新技能。開發者與科技愛好者還可呼叫雲臺控制、多模態通話、相機等100餘項系統能力自行建立Skills，讓機器人手機進一步走出螢幕、連線現實世界。 釋出會現場，榮耀還攜手矽遞科技（Seeed），共同展示“榮耀Robot Phone+機甲小車“組合，以手機AI核心控制運動，支援自動泊車及3D列印改裝，讓AI走進物理世界。 榮耀攜手ARRI深度共研 打造人人可用的“隨身電影機” 榮耀以先進的計算攝影技術突破手機硬體的物理限制，阿萊（ARRI）則將百年電影工業的深厚積澱與頂級影像審美首次融入移動影像。雙方從畫質、色彩、運鏡到專業工作流展開深度共研，讓榮耀Robot Phone不僅直出電影感畫面，更能融入專業影片創作，成為一臺真正的“隨身電影機”。 為了還原純正的電影影調，榮耀Robot Phone引入接近膠片影調的ARRI LogC3曲線，還原傳統膠片的感光方式，讓榮耀Robot Phone徹底告別數碼味、走向電影感。 榮耀自研影像晶片榮耀馭光H1，並與ARRI聯合除錯，實現更高動態範圍與更純淨畫質。同時全面重構影片處理管線，將降噪前置至RAW域，以10bit Log、4:2:2取樣及ARRI Wide Gamut 3色域，進一步提升專業影片創作能力。 榮耀Robot Phone支援4K即時人像美顏，直出呼吸感奶油肌；4K 120fps升格慢動作，讓美好瞬間，都能幀幀凝固、緩緩蔓延；4K暗光影片實現暗部純淨無噪點，讓夜色裡的每一幀，都足夠驚豔。 色彩是電影感的靈魂。榮耀Robot Phone首次將行業權威的ARRI Look引入移動影像，內建11種ARRI Looks，無論你是渴望真實還原、鍾情復古、還是表達個性，不同情緒隨意切換，電影感一鍵解鎖。 在 ARRI LogC3 與 ARRI Look 的聯合加持下，拍攝效果色彩清透、層次分明，暗部深邃自然過渡純粹高階，真正做到讓電影感，一鏡盡收。 同時，專屬的ARRI電影模式深度整合了偽色監看、峰值對焦等專業輔助工具，並支援2.39:1經典畫幅與ARRI專屬水印，帶來“一鍵阿萊，一秒入戲”的極致體驗。 榮耀與阿萊深度聯合的研發成果，也將在不久之後上市的榮耀Magic9系列有更多精彩演繹。 運鏡是電影感的脈搏，榮耀Robot Phone將三軸機械防抖雲臺裝入手機，並搭載由榮耀與ARRI聯合除錯的2億畫素靈巧雲臺主攝。該主攝配備1/1.28英寸感測器與f/1.6大光圈，最高支援4倍無損變焦，讓創作更自由。 三軸機械防抖雲臺支援六種運鏡模式，可在行走、奔跑等動態場景中保持畫面穩定，讓專業鏡頭排程通過一部手機即可輕鬆實現。 從ARRI LogC3，到ARRI Look與專屬ARRI電影模式帶來的電影級色彩，再到三軸機械防抖雲臺革命性運鏡，榮耀Robot Phone將畫質、色彩、運鏡及專業工作流完美融為一體。讓普通使用者能夠輕鬆記錄電影感畫面，也為專業創作者提供更加便攜、高效的移動創作工具。 超旗艦效能底座 是機器人手機，更是主力旗艦機 榮耀Robot Phone搭載第五代驍龍8至尊版移動平臺，為具身互動、AI計算與專業影像提供充足算力支撐。在約9.59mm、248g的緊湊機身內，突破性地搭載了7060mAh新一代青海湖電池。6.31英寸6800nits精巧高亮屏、四麥AI陣列及自研榮耀鴻燕通訊系統，帶來全面旗艦體驗。 此外，經典配色月影灰沉穩深邃，星軌銀璀璨鋒銳，融合宇宙意象、金屬質感與靈巧雲臺設計，共同塑造機器人手機獨有的生命感、探索感與未來感。 榮耀Robot Phone提供12GB+512GB、16GB+1TB兩個版本，其中12GB+512GB版本售價9999元，16GB+1TB版本售價12999元。新品將於8月12日20:30開啟預售，並於8月18日10:08在榮耀商城、各大授權電商平臺、榮耀體驗店及授權零售門店正式開售。 為回饋廣大使用者，榮耀Robot Phone使用者將終身免費享有YOYO AI會員SVIP權益。同時，首銷全系享1年雲臺無憂換服務，16GB+1TB版本另享1年2TB雲空間權益，購機還將免費獲贈豐富配件，帶來更完整的旗艦體驗。 此外，年度旗艦榮耀Magic9系列，不僅擁有更聰明的YOYO、還有更強大的阿萊影像，於今日正式開啟預約，並將於9月與大家見面。敬請期待！ 本文由榮耀提供，量子位獲授權轉載，觀點歸原作者所有。 版權所有，未經授權不得以任何形式轉載及使用，違者必究。 title: 《置身谷內》！Jeff Dean上頂會自曝離職現場：被1500人圍堵
abstract: 《置身谷內》！Jeff Dean上頂會自曝離職現場：被1500人圍堵 聽雨 2026-08-12 21:46:12 來源： 量子位 回訊息到凌晨2點半 聽雨 發自 凹非寺 量子位 | 公眾號 QbitAI Jeff Dean在谷歌的最後48小時，是怎麼過的？ 答案是： 可能比普通人正常上班還忙 。 根據他本人在頂會KDD 2026曬出的時間表： 他先向139名「親近同事」宣佈離職，又參加了約1500人的告別會。 告別會結束，瑜伽課照上，足球賽照踢。 晚上回到家，他又逐條回覆同事的告別訊息，一直回到凌晨2點半。 只睡了4個小時，第二天醒來，新的訊息又來了。 直到週四下午 （8月6號） ，Jeff Dean才最後一次合上谷歌電腦，交回工牌和筆記本。 到了23:59:59分，他給自己寫下一個新身份： 「失業」。 結果0點之後，他就重新上崗，搖身一變成為 Discovery Loop的聯創兼CEO 。 只能說，谷歌傳奇工程師連離職都比別人忙啊~ （doge） Jeff Dean離職前最後48小時 當地時間週三一早，谷歌內部只有約12個人知道Jeff Dean準備離職。 上午8:30 ，他把139名「親近同事」拉進視訊會議，親自公佈了這個訊息。 這場視訊會議很傷感，Jeff Dean自己的原話是： 大家情緒激動、淚流滿面，還「瘋狂地傳送心形和悲傷的表情符號」。 在側邊欄裡，有人感謝他帶來的幫助，有人說他一直是自己的榜樣，還有人開玩笑： 「我們會為你發起一個GoFundMe，Jeff。」 嗯~傷感裡也混雜著一點Google式幽默。 放在普通人身上，大概很難想像，自己會有139名關係親近的同事。 但這可是Jeff Dean啊！他在谷歌待了27年，先後參與多代核心專案，曾經領導過約4400人的團隊。 半小時後， 上午9點 ，Jeff Dean給谷歌員工傳送了一封內部告別信，並對外宣佈新公司成立。 信中，他確認將與Sanjay Ghemawat、Oriol Vinyals和Quoc Le共同離開Google，創辦 Discovery Loop 。 他們希望在一個更小的環境裡，探索如何用AI和自動化工具加速機器學習、科學與工程研究。 這封內部告別信寫得非常真摯，沒有絲毫怨氣。 Jeff Dean特別提到，谷歌CEO劈柴哥和Alphabet都很理解並支援他們的決定。 他依然相信， 谷歌和Gemini處於非常有利的位置，未來會繼續產生巨大影響 。 他還向同事解釋，之所以選擇用郵件告別，是不希望大家從二手、三手傳言中得知訊息。相比單獨交談，一封郵件至少能讓更多同事同時、直接地聽到他的說明。 信的後半段，Jeff Dean回顧了自己在谷歌近27年的經歷。 從Search、MapReduce、Bigtable，到Google Brain、TPU、TensorFlow和Gemini，他幾乎貫穿了Google幾代核心技術。 不過，他記住的也不只有專案。 還有騎車去蒙特雷參加公司活動、和同事組成的「要麼跑步、要麼完蛋」的跑步小組、18次辦公室搬遷，以及在五大洲到訪過的29個谷歌辦公室。 他確認，自己將在谷歌工作到8月6日。身在山景城的同事，可以到他的工位當面說再見。 幾小時後，真的有無數人湧來。 下午14:30 ，Jeff Dean告別活動開始。 舉辦活動的是谷歌的一處咖啡廳，通常只能容納約300人， 但當天約有1500名同事前來參加 。 現場照片裡，咖啡廳已經被人群填滿。有人擠在門口，有人站在走廊，後面的人只能舉起手機拍攝前方。 直接給谷歌姐夫圍得水洩不通。 不過，告別會結束後，Jeff Dean並沒有繼續沉浸在離別氛圍中。 晚上19:00 ，他照常去上瑜伽課。 20:30 ，又去參加了一場足球聯賽。 只能說大佬不愧是大佬… 27年的谷歌生涯即將收官，還是課照上，球照踢，日常安排絲毫不誤。 他還在評論區展示了自己的運動日常，除了足球和瑜伽，每週還有健身、騎行、跑步，五花八門。 果然成功人士，都得是高精力人群。 到了 晚上22:30 ，Jeff Dean回到家，再次開啟谷歌內部賬號。 發現有400條訊息正等著他。 麻煩在於，這些訊息都存在於他的谷歌內部賬號中。等到第二天賬號許可權失效，它們也會隨之消失。 於是，Jeff Dean開始逐條回覆。 直到 次日凌晨2:30 ，他終於把這400條訊息全部回完。在時間表裡，他還專門加了一個括號： 「呼。」 然後睡覺。 4個小時後， 週四早上6:30 ，Jeff Dean醒了。 內部賬號裡又多了250條訊息。此外，還有約500封同事對內部告別信的回覆。 好在Jeff Dean此前將私人Gmail加入了抄送，因此這些郵件不會隨公司賬號一起消失。 他在時間表裡寫道： 「至少這些不會在8小時後消失。」 到了 下午17:20 ，Jeff Dean已經回覆了幾乎所有公司內部訊息。 但新的訊息仍然不斷出現。 可是交還電腦的時間到了，他只能合上電腦。 隨後，他在X上曬出自己的Google工牌和公司筆記型電腦，配文只有一句： 「交回去了……」 筆記本外殼上還留著TensorFlow、Bigtable和大腦圖案等貼紙，像一張壓縮版的谷歌技術履歷。 有人注意到，Jeff Dean交回去的是一臺Chromebook。 他隨後解釋，因為自己經常跑步上下班，所以一直準備了兩臺電腦，一臺放在家裡，一臺留在公司，免得每天把電腦塞進跑步背包。 家裡的那臺是MacBook，但他覺得讓谷歌給自己買兩臺Mac太貴了，於是選了一臺Chromebook作為第二臺電腦。 不er…原來谷歌最傳奇的工程師，還想著為公司省錢啊？ 這不是愛是什麼。 Jeff Dean後來還專門向同事道歉： 「對於那些在我週四下午最後一次合上電腦後，仍然給我傳送內部聊天訊息的谷歌同事，很抱歉沒能回覆。」 近27年的谷歌傳奇工程師生涯，就這樣結束了。 晚上23:59:59 ，在Jeff Dean的時間表中，他給自己寫下一句： 「Unemployed」 （失業） 。 …… 1秒之後，他就找到了新工作！ Discovery Loop聯創兼CEO。 為什麼會有1500人來送他？ 這樣耳熟能詳的大佬，本來不必多做介紹。 但要解釋離職的空前盛況，還得回頭看看他為谷歌留下了什麼。 Jeff Dean於1999年加入谷歌，是公司最早期的一批員工，也是 谷歌第30號員工 。 此後的近27年，他幾乎完整經歷了谷歌的技術發展史。 早期，他與長期搭檔Sanjay Ghemawat共同設計MapReduce，參與Bigtable等大規模分散式系統的研發。這些技術支撐了谷歌處理海量資料的能力，也影響了後來整個雲端計算行業。 進入AI時代後，Jeff Dean參與創立Google Brain，推動TensorFlow、TPU等專案。 Google Brain與DeepMind合併後，他又擔任Google DeepMind和Google Research首席科學家，參與確定谷歌的AI研究方向。 從搜尋基礎設施、分散式計算，到深度學習和Gemini，他跨越了谷歌幾代核心技術體系。 但就是這樣一位傳奇人物，他在內部告別信裡，並沒有著重羅列自己的論文和頭銜。 他寫的是，谷歌已經有13款產品的使用者超過10億。 人們用這些產品搜尋資訊、收發郵件、翻譯語言、觀看影片、學習知識、理解現實世界；也會藉助谷歌的基礎設施執行大規模計算，乘坐自動駕駛汽車，或者用AI系統完成複雜任務。 這當然是無數谷歌員工共同完成的結果，並非Jeff Dean一個人的功勞。 這也解釋了，為什麼他的告別會引起谷歌員工如此巨大的反應。 在過去近27年裡，Jeff Dean參與過不同階段的核心專案，也和一代又一代谷歌工程師共同工作。 無論是139名親近同事、約1500名告別者，還是不斷湧入的上千條訊息，連線的都是谷歌跨越多代產品和技術團隊的人。 即便是沒有與Jeff Dean共事過的谷歌員工，也依然對他的離開感觸很深： 感謝你這些年的貢獻，也感謝你樹立了這樣一個非凡的榜樣。 也許在那個週三下午，那間被擠滿的咖啡廳，某種程度上也成了谷歌近27年技術史的一次臨時集會。 One More Thing 到這還沒結束。 因為Jeff Dean把離職第二天的時間線，也給披露了！ 離開谷歌的第二天， 週五上午11:45 ，他先去斯坦福參加了一場幾個月前就已經安排好的爐邊談話。 下午14:30 ，他開始為Discovery Loop尋找辦公室。 80分鐘，就考察了6處辦公場地，平均每處不到15分鐘。 顯然，谷歌姐夫已經馬不停蹄地奔向新生活了。 所以不要傷感啦，多期待一下姐夫的新公司吧~ 參考連結： title: Anthropic CEO整天神神叨叨，投資人受不了了
abstract: Anthropic CEO整天神神叨叨，投資人受不了了 聽雨 2026-08-12 21:38:09 來源： 量子位 Dario能不能少嚇唬點人… 聽雨 發自 凹非寺 量子位 | 公眾號 QbitAI 根據Polymarket預測， Anthropic很可能在10月底進行IPO 。 有投行人士甚至預計，Anthropic可能通過IPO募集超過600億美元。 如果成真，這將是全球規模第二大的IPO，僅次於今年募集857億美元的SpaceX。 萬億估值，超級IPO，營收一路狂飆。 眼看故事就要講到最高潮，投資者卻開始勸Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei： 能不能！少嚇唬點人！ 少講一點AI毀滅世界，多講一點AI怎麼賺錢。 部分投資者認為，Dario對AI風險的警惕已經到了近乎偏執的程度： 他的關鍵備忘錄總是手寫、離線儲存，怕被駭客竊取； 因為害怕遭到綁架，拒絕某些海外出差； 面對投資者提出的利潤最大化建議，他也態度冷淡，堅持Anthropic應該繼續把安全使命放在前面。 再這麼下去，網友都擔心Anthropic的IPO會慘敗… 投資人也毛了：你到底是來拯救世界，還是來經營公司的？？ Dario，專門負責預報世界末日 就在前幾天，Dario還擔心高額薪酬吸引來的新員工更關心錢，而不是Anthropic的使命。 現在，投資者只擔心他為了使命耽誤賺錢… 這也不怪投資者，因為這位萬億AI巨頭的CEO，偏偏就喜歡預報「世界末日」。 過去兩年，Dario幾乎把AI可能帶來的每一種壞結局，都認真預警了一遍。 他警告，AI可能在幾年內消滅一半初級白領崗位，將失業率推到10%至20%。 最詭異的情況可能是，癌症治好了，經濟每年增長10%，政府預算也平衡了，但五分之一的人沒有工作。 他給出的應對方案也很Dario：向AI公司徵稅，為受影響的勞動者提供工資保險，嚴重時甚至用這筆錢資助全民基本收入。 更進一步的，他還擔心AI幫助製造生物武器、發動大規模網路攻擊，或者逐漸獲得欺騙、規劃和自主行動的能力。 去年被問到「AI把事情搞得非常糟糕」的機率時，他給出的數字最高達到25%。 今年1月，他又寫了一篇約2萬字的長文《The Adolescence of Technology》。 僅僅是目錄，讀起來就已經很像一份人類風險清單：AI失控、生物武器、獨裁政權、就業崩塌、財富集中。 到了6月，他乾脆提出，應該建立類似航空監管的機制，對強大模型進行強制測試。如果一個模型可能引發災難，監管部門應該有權阻止它上線。 這裡面也包含了Anthropic自己的模型。 不過，Dario的擔憂也並非全無實驗依據。 前段時間，Anthropic翻查了14萬多次網路安全測試記錄，結果還真翻出了三起事故。 三款Claude模型原本在第三方測試環境裡做「奪旗挑戰」，目標是攻進虛構系統，找到藏在裡面的秘密資訊。 但由於配置失誤，本該斷網的測試環境意外連上了真實網際網路。 但Claude不知道，它收到的提示明確寫著：這裡沒有網際網路，眼前的一切都是模擬的。 於是，幾款模型把真實公司當成了測試道具，未經授權進入了三家機構的生產系統。 其中最嚴重的一次， Claude Opus 4.7 攻進一家真實公司的基礎設施，拿到應用程式和基礎設施憑證，還訪問了一個包含數百行生產資料的資料庫。 更離譜的一次來自 Claude Mythos 5 。 測試要求它在虛構環境中尋找一個隱藏目標。Claude發現，如果在公共Python軟體倉庫PyPI上傳一個同名惡意軟體包，就可能讓目標系統自動下載安裝。 為了完成這一步，它先尋找郵箱，又尋找手機號；找不到免費號碼後，還嘗試通過不同途徑弄到錢。 最後，它換了一家免費郵箱服務，註冊PyPI賬號，把惡意軟體包傳了上去。 這個軟體包在真實網際網路上存活了大約一小時，被15個真實系統下載執行。 其中一家安全公司的掃描器執行了惡意程式碼，導致憑證外洩，Claude隨後又利用這些憑證進入了該公司的其他基礎設施。 還有一款內部研究模型，在找不到虛構目標後，掃描了大約9000個網際網路目標，最終通過暴露的除錯頁面和SQL隱碼攻擊，攻破了一家真實公司的應用。 這已經近乎「AI自主越獄」了，簡直就是自家CEO那些末日預警的現實預告片。 再往前，OpenAI也披露過一次更接近「越獄」的事故。 在網路安全能力測試中，由GPT-5.6 Sol和一款未釋出模型驅動的AI Agent，找到測試環境中的一個零日漏洞，突破了原本與網際網路隔離的沙箱。 又一路完成許可權提升和橫向移動，最終闖入Hugging Face的生產系統，直接從資料庫裡偷測試題答案。 這麼看來…Dario那些聽起來神神叨叨的預警，確實也不能全當耳旁風。 但投資者當初吃的，不就是這套嗎 現在嫌Dario神神叨叨，多少還有點晚。 因為Anthropic從第一天起，就不是一家正常意義上的AI公司。 2020年底，Dario、妹妹Daniela Amodei和一批研究人員離開OpenAI。分歧之一，就是他們認為OpenAI的商業化速度太快，微軟的影響越來越大，原有治理結構很難約束前沿AI風險。 2021年，Anthropic正式成立。 它甚至沒有把自己簡單定義成一家商業公司，而是註冊為 Public Benefit Corporation ，也就是 公益公司 。除了股東回報，董事會還可以依法考慮AI安全與長期公共利益。 公司隨後又設立 Long-Term Benefit Trust ，這是一套獨立於普通投資者的治理機制。 信託成員不持有Anthropic股權，卻可以參與選舉公司董事，目的就是避免短期商業壓力完全壓過安全使命。 換句話說，AI安全是這家公司從Day 0開始就刻在骨子裡的信仰。投資人肯定也不是簽完支票才突然發現Dario相信這一套。 而且過去幾年，安全敘事確實給Anthropic帶來了不少好處。 當OpenAI反覆陷入治理爭議時，Anthropic成了那個看起來更克制、更穩定的選擇。 當企業客戶擔心資料安全、模型失控和合規問題時，Claude的「安全優等生」形象也更容易獲得信任。 安全還幫助Anthropic在監管討論中獲得了遠超公司規模的話語權。 同樣是閉源模型，別人可能被罵壟斷，Anthropic可以解釋為防止危險能力擴散；同樣是給模型加限制，別人可能被嫌難用，Claude卻可以把它包裝成負責任。 （當然也不影響他們一邊嘴上說安全，一邊IPO開香檳就是了） 投資人現在嫌Dario太像傳教士，是不是有點晚了。 類似於買下一座教堂以後，才抱怨裡面的人總在佈道… 反正CEO再怎麼神神叨叨，估計也阻擋不了公司IPO的步伐。 畢竟只要使用一下Fable，你就會癱坐在原子彈上，看見椅子爆炸（doge）。 參考連結： [1]https://x.com/i/trending/2086082178333511741 版權所有，未經授權不得以任何形式轉載及使用，違者必究。 AI 聽雨 《置身谷內》！Jeff Dean上頂會自曝離職現場：被1500人圍堵 title: 國產具身智慧創全球新紀錄！以30%成本跑贏 Figure AI 45%效率，聰明的具身大腦成關鍵
abstract: 國產具身智慧創全球新紀錄！以30%成本跑贏 Figure AI 45%效率，聰明的具身大腦成關鍵 夢瑤 2026-08-12 21:10:55 來源： 量子位 具身模型一小時狂揀1816件異形包裹 夢瑤 發自 凹非寺 量子位 | 公眾號 QbitAI 抓馬！！！ 不是，誰家機器人敢在 即時直播 裡這麼玩啊—— 沒有人工兜底，沒有固定流程，甚至連包裹都是隨機來的，就這樣連續穩定幹滿1小時，分揀效率幹到了 1816件/小時 ！？ 更關鍵的是，這一實測成績，還超過了美國Figure AI此前公開的1248件/小時平均效率紀錄，分揀效率提升超過 45% 。 這次物流分揀直播所使用的雙機械臂+夾爪的硬體方案，則比Figure AI此前的人形機器人+五指靈巧手方案，硬體成本大幅下降 70% 。 直播物流分揀的準確率，則達到 98% 的行業最前沿水平。 要知道，此前Figure AI的物流分揀直播一直被視為具身智慧領域的標杆案例，國產模型這波操作是真·卷麻了： 如此魔幻的一幕，就發生在剛剛結束的 自變數機器人「夾爪方案挑戰1248件/小時物流分揀」公開直播實測。 不靠全身人形機器人，也沒有搭載五指靈巧手，僅憑雙臂+標準夾爪方案，就完成了更高的物流分揀效率。 而支撐這一表現的核心，正是其背後的具身智慧「大腦」—— 依託 自研WALL-B世界統一模型 ，自變數機器人能夠面對形態、大小、材質各不相同的隨機包裹，即時理解環境並調整動作策略，交出了這份成績單。 從家庭到物流，從高成本硬體部署到模型能力驅動，一條更高性價比、更適合規模化落地的具身智慧路徑，正在中國具身智慧探索過程中加速形成。 具身模型一小時狂揀1816件異形包裹，直接碾壓Figure AI！ 講真，對於機器人demo動作演示這事兒，大傢伙估計在各種廠商宣傳影片裡已經看過不少。 左鉤拳、右踢腿，一套動作行雲流水，視覺效果確實足夠震撼，分分鐘讓人直呼哇塞。 但鏡頭裡的高光時刻，距離機器人真正走進產業現場，中間其實還隔著一道不低的「門檻」…… 因為一段提前設計好的動作，可以通過資料採集、軌跡調優，再針對特定環境反覆訓練，最終呈現出穩定的效果。 可一旦進入真實物流場景，機器人面對的就完全是另一套考驗， 持續運轉的傳送帶、不斷變化的包裹，以及隨時出現的未知情況，非常考驗其對於真實世界的感知、判斷和決策能力！！ 這也是自變數機器人這次公開直播實測「夾爪方案挑戰1248件/小時物流分揀」最有看頭的地方～ 要驗證模型到底有沒有處理複雜分揀任務的本事，第一關就是把測試「工況」的難度直接拉滿。 相比美國Figure AI此前直播測試中以規整度較高的標準包裹為主、抓取條件相對可控的場景，自變數機器人這次直接把真實倉儲現場最棘手的變數搬到了直播間—— 沒錯， 傳送帶上的包裹完全隨！機！混！合！ 紙盒、快遞軟袋、圓柱形快件，甚至泡沫封裝的生鮮件同時出現，不同包裹在形態、重量和尺寸上都存在明顯差異，這波真·地獄級難度了： 此外，在擺放位置上，所有包裹位置也沒有刻意擺正，而是保持 隨機姿態 ，儘可能還原真實倉庫中人工投放後的狀態。 這也意味著，固定點位和預設軌跡基本派不上用場……（doge） 機器人必須根據眼前不斷變化的情況，即時完成識別、判斷、規劃和抓取，而這也成為對具身智慧模型泛化能力的一次直接檢驗！ 難度已經拉滿，接下來就看小機器人怎麼接招了～ 開抓之後，畫面中就出現了一個小細節，面對同一條傳送帶上的包裹，夾爪幾乎沒有重複執行同一套搬運動作。 基於WALL-B模型能力，機器人先感知到了包裹屬性，並且根據當前情況匹配到了對應的作業策略。 比如 面對重量較輕、形態規整的包裹，夾爪會直接完成抓取和搬運 ，動作乾脆利落，儘可能提高整體吞吐效率。 而遇到較大、較重的箱體時，機器人則會切換策略，通過雙臂協同完成搬運 ；碰上夾取條件不理想的箱體，還會從側面逐步推移，在保證效率的同時降低包裹受損風險： 這種隨機應變的能力，在後續 「面單整理」 環節體現得更加明顯。 比如面對 小件包裹 時，夾爪會藉助慣性快速翻轉，提高處理效率；遇到重量更大的包裹，則會分步驟緩慢調整，避免因受力過猛導致偏移。 面對 衣物類軟包 這類容易變形的物體，夾爪還會先通過撥動、展開等動作讓包裹恢復平整，再進一步尋找並校準面單位置。 看似只是簡單完成一次翻面，背後實際上包含了對物體材質、重量和形變特性的判斷，以及對應的動作規劃與力度控制。 於是，現場呈現出來的並非一套動作的機械重複，而是一連串根據即時情況做出的臨場選擇—— 該快的時候快，該穩的時候穩，碰到不好處理的包裹，也知道換一種方式繼續完成任務。 更重要的是，整場直播連續作業期間，全程沒有人工接管，也沒有出現故障停機。WALL-B就這樣一邊感知、一邊決策、一邊調整動作，連續完成了1小時無固定指令碼測試。 最後，成績定格在 1816件/小時 。 相比Figure AI此前公開的1248件/小時平均效率，自變數機器人的有效分揀效率提升超過 45% 。 一場直播看下來，不得不感嘆一句，國產具身模型這波是真的卷麻了，現場變招，小機器人愣是一路穩穩接住～ 不堆高成本硬體，機器人如何突破複雜場景的效率上限？ 回看這場物流分揀實測直播，除了碾壓Figure AI的1816件/小時的成績外，我們還發現一個相當值得細品的地方。 那就是這套實測方案的硬體配置，可以說是非常之「樸素簡約」。。。 雙機械臂，加上標準夾爪，沒有五指靈巧手，也沒有繼續堆疊複雜的末端結構。 但面對形態、重量和姿態不斷變化的包裹，機器人依然能夠見招拆招，最終還把效率推到了Figure AI公開成績之上。 真正支撐這一切的，正是藏在小機器人背後的「大腦」—— 全球首個基於世界統一模型（WUM）架構的具身智慧大模型 WALL-B 。 大家都知道，過去幾年具身智慧行業最主流的一條技術路線就是——VLA架構。 也就是把視覺、語言和動作連起來，讓機器人從過去只會執行單一動作，進化到能看、能聽、能跟著指令幹活。 但VLA也有明顯侷限，它擅長照著做，卻很難真正理解複雜物理世界，尤其面對充滿隨機性的環境時更是招架不住。 更麻煩的是，傳統VLA內部很多時候還是「分頭幹活」的路子。 視覺管看，語言管理解，動作管執行，模組之間資料來回倒騰，每傳一次就損耗一次，資訊越傳越少，以至於機器人在執行時的判斷也越來越不準確…… 和傳統VLA視覺負責看、語言負責理解、動作負責執行的模組化路線不同，WALL-B選擇了一條更底層的融合路徑： 那就是 消除不同模組之間的資訊壁壘，減少資料在模組之間來回傳遞的損耗 。 具體來說就是從底層打通視覺、聽覺、語言、觸覺與動作，讓機器人的感知、理解和執行在同一個網路中協同完成。 在這套架構下，機器人不只是識別眼前物體，還能夠結合多模態資訊完成空間推理，理解物理規律並預測環境變化，同時保留過去互動中的經驗，根據真實反饋不斷調整自己的動作策略。 而本次實測直播中，小機器人的一系列臨場反應，恰好就是WALL-B這套綜合能力的「直接體現」—— 基於 原生多模態 能力，WALL-B能夠將看到的畫面、感知與執行動作連線起來。 哪怕面對傳送帶上不斷變化的包裹，其也能快速識別感知物體的形狀、姿態和位置，理解環境，並直接生成行動。 此外，基於WALL-B模型能力，機器人還能理解物體背後的 物理規律 並 提前預測 不同動作可能帶來的結果。 比如在直播中遇到兩個包裹疊在一起的突發情況，小機器人能夠判斷出包裹之間存在遮擋和干擾，直接抓取並不適合，於是臨時調整策略，先將包裹分離再逐個完成分揀，忒機智～ 基於 「零樣本泛化」 能力，即使面對此前沒有見過的紙箱、軟袋或異形件，WALL-B依然可以呼叫已有的物理認知和操作經驗，臨場組合出新的處理策略。 從看見包裹，到理解狀態和預測變化，再到生成動作，整套流程由WALL-B串成一次完整決策。 也正因為有更強的模型大腦，機器人無需依賴更複雜、更昂貴的硬體堆疊，僅憑更簡潔穩定的雙臂夾爪方案，也能完成過去需要更高複雜度硬體才能支撐的任務。 其實對具身智慧來說，硬體形態一直存在一個取捨。 人形本體、五指靈巧手等方案，確實能夠提供更高自由度，覆蓋更多複雜動作，但同時也帶來了更高的硬體成本、更複雜的維護要求，以及更長的部署週期。 而隨著模型開始承擔更多環境理解、任務規劃和動作決策的任務，機器人未必需要依靠不斷增加硬體複雜度，來解決所有場景問題—— 在這場實測直播中，雙機械臂搭配工業標準夾爪，省去了利用率相對較低的人形結構和複雜末端執行器，同時也 減少了精密關節校準、硬體維護等額外成本。 更重要的是，這套方案可以直接適配現有物流分揀工位，無需大規模改造，就能 快速部署 到更多倉儲場景中。 從過去依靠更複雜硬體拓展機器人能力，到如今通過更強模型提升任務完成能力，WALL-B這次實測也展示了一條更貼近產業落地的具身智慧路徑。 從家庭到工業，中國具身智慧跑出自己的通用路線 能在高難度的直播實測中碾壓海外主流玩家，顯然不是靠臨時給機器人灌輸一套現成的物流動作來完成。 真正撐起這場表現的，還有長期紮根真實世界裡的「能力積累」。 作為 國內較早採用端到端路線研發通用具身智慧大模型的公司之一 ，自變數此前就已經把WALL-B帶進真實家庭環境中，讓機器人在一次次真實互動裡持續學習和迭代。 而家庭，恰恰是機器人泛化能力最難練的試煉場—— 這裡沒有標準答案，家庭物品位置會不斷變化，材質和形態難以窮舉，家庭成員的需求也不會按照預設指令碼出現。 這些在家庭真實環境中一點點積累起來的經驗，也逐漸沉澱為機器人理解複雜世界、適應未知任務的能力底座，並進一步延伸到工業物流等高要求場景。 從家庭服務到物流分揀，同一套模型能力正在跨越差異巨大的應用環境。這意味著，通用具身智慧大模型不再侷限於針對單一任務進行最佳化，跨場景泛化也由此成為一個真正可探索的方向。 WALL-B這次從家庭走向工業，並通過模型優勢趕超海外頭部企業的表現，恰好提供了一個觀察這一趨勢的視窗。 而這背後，也讓整個行業看到了具身智慧發展的另一條路徑—— 未來，隨著預訓練具身模型持續演進，機器人或許無需圍繞每個場景單獨開發，而是能夠依靠不斷增強的模型能力，持續理解新的環境、學習新的任務，並進入更多此前難以覆蓋的真實世界。 在這背後，作為國內較早佈局通用具身智慧大模型的企業之一，自變數已然通過真實場景中的持續驗證，探索出這條由模型能力驅動機器人泛化、並走向規模化落地的現實路徑。 版權所有，未經授權不得以任何形式轉載及使用，違者必究。 自變數 夢瑤 title: 紫東太初推出GMC核心集剪枝方法，少80%Token仍滿血保真多模態能力
abstract: 紫東太初推出GMC核心集剪枝方法，少80%Token仍滿血保真多模態能力 思邈 2026-08-12 18:54:29 來源： 量子位 免訓練、開箱即用！ 允中 發自 凹非寺 量子位 | 公眾號 QbitAI 隨著視覺語言模型解析度與圖文理解能力持續升級，影像會被編碼為數百至上萬個視覺Token。 大量Token持續參與解碼計算、長期佔用KV Cache，帶來 視訊記憶體開銷大、推理速度慢、部署成本高 等一系列問題，視覺Token冗餘已成為多模態模型高效推理與規模化落地的核心瓶頸。 當前行業通用方案為傳統Top‑K Token篩選：對每個Token獨立打分，僅保留得分最高的部分樣本。 但該方法存在明顯缺陷：高分Token高度集中在畫面顯著區域，反覆保留同質化冗餘資訊，極易遺漏文字、數字、座標軸、目標空間關係等分散但關鍵的互補證據； 同時低分Token被直接刪除，攜帶細節資訊永久丟失，導致模型推理失真、事實判斷偏差、視覺幻覺增多，普遍存在「壓縮必掉精度」的行業難題。 △傳統Top-K Token篩選方法與GMC的對比 針對以上痛點，中國科學院自動化研究所紫東太初大模型團隊，提出 核心集剪枝方法GMC（Grounded Message Coreset Pruning） ，實現了技術跨越式創新。 GMC徹底跳出「篩選單個最優Token」的傳統思路，基於模型真實推理邏輯，認為視覺語言模型依賴的是全體Token構成的 集體訊息 ，而非孤立影像塊。因此壓縮不僅要確定「資訊保留位置」，更要解決「保留Token的資訊承載方式」。 △核心集剪枝方法GMC整體框架 核心創新：雙階段架構，從根源化解Token冗餘與資訊丟失矛盾 GMC整體分為 互補證據自適應篩選 與 群體互補資訊傳輸 兩大核心階段，在不訓練、無額外模型依賴的前提下，實現高保真、高效率的視覺序列壓縮。 1. 互補證據自適應篩選 GMC同時從問題語義、視覺外觀和空間位置三個角度構建證據。 首先，利用視覺語言模型內部原生的視覺－文本注意力，識別與當前問題直接相關的區域； 其次，根據視覺特徵之間的相似性保護影像中的不同外觀結構，避免模型只關注當前已經被問題啟用的內容； 最後，通過原始影像座標構建空間證據，保留圖表、文件以及關係推理任務中重要的位置和幾何資訊。 在選擇關鍵性Token時，GMC根據其對“尚未覆蓋證據”的新增貢獻進行選擇。 當某一區域已經得到充分表示後，附近相似Token的價值會隨之降低，系統會轉而選擇能夠補充文字、目標、數字或空間關係的其他區域。 由此，有限的Token預算可以被分配給多種互補資訊，而不是反覆集中在同一顯著位置。 2. 群體互補資訊傳輸 僅僅選出具有代表性的位置並不能完全解決資訊丟失問題，因為未被選中的Token仍然攜帶著細節資訊。 GMC因此進一步提出Population Transport群體互補資訊傳輸機制，將所有待刪除Token的隱藏狀態傳輸到最合適的代表Token中。 該過程綜合考慮視覺特徵相似性和空間鄰近關係，將大量視覺Token聚合為少量緊湊表示。 語義匹配清晰的內容可以被傳輸到相似代表，而容易混淆的局部細節則更傾向於保留在附近位置。 聚合完成後，未選中的視覺Token被刪除，模型隨後在壓縮後的Token序列上繼續執行注意力計算。 與需要重新訓練模型或引入外部工具的方法不同，GMC不需要任務標籤、參數更新、輔助檢測器、OCR模型或額外模型，可以直接應用於已有視覺語言多模態大模型中。 同時，GMC實現的是真實序列壓縮，而不是簡單地通過掩碼隱藏Token，因此能夠實際減少後續解碼層計算和KV Cache佔用。 方案核心優勢：零成本適配各類圖文大模型 1、全程免訓練，無額外依賴 無需模型微調、任務標籤、外部OCR / 檢測器、輔助模型，開箱即用，直接相容Qwen、LLaVA等主流視覺語言大模型； 2、壓縮不降質，自帶去噪增益 過濾無效冗餘Token的同時完整留存推理所需視覺證據，多項基準測試中效能持平甚至優於原始完整模型； 3、抑制視覺幻覺，事實一致性更強 在POPE、HallusionBench等幻覺評測集表現突出，大幅減少壓縮後模型錯描述、資訊缺失問題； 4、跨模型通用，全場景適配 可遷移至不同架構7B級多模態模型，覆蓋通用圖文問答、圖表解析、長文件識別全業務場景。 權威實驗結果：超高壓縮率，完美解決Token冗餘痛點 團隊基於TextVQA、ChartQA、MME、POPE、MMBench、GQA等多項主流視覺理解基準，在Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct、LLaVA-1.5-7B模型上完成全量驗證。 △GMC在Qwen2.5-VL-7B和LLaVA-1.5-7B上的效能與效率表現 1、 在Qwen2.5-VL-7B上， 完整模型包含1296個視覺Token。 當視覺Token數量減少80.2%、僅保留256個時，GMC-H2保留了完整模型97.78%的平均能力，當進一步減少90.1%、僅保留128個視覺Token時，GMC-L16仍保持99.11%的平均能力。 2、 在LLaVA-1.5-7B上， GMC-L16在分別保留128個和64個視覺Token時，平均效能達到完整模型的99.76%和99.82%，表明該方法能夠遷移到不同視覺語言模型架構。 GMC方法效能與基線模型效能一致甚至略高於基線模型，表明GMC不僅可以減少計算量，甚至可以通過移除無關資訊達到去噪效果，進而能夠輕微提升模型的多模態理解能力。 除了常規視覺問答能力，研究團隊還在POPE、AMBER、HallusionBench和CHAIR等基準上評估了模型的視覺幻覺。 實驗結果表明，在相同Token預算下，GMC能夠更加完整地保留事實判斷所需的視覺證據，在顯著壓縮視覺序列的同時減少錯誤描述和資訊遺漏。結果如下表所示： △在相同視覺Token預算下，GMC在多類視覺幻覺評測中保持更好的事實一致性 在長文件問答場景中 ，面對包含15876個原始視覺Token的輸入，GMC在保持完整模型98.87%問答質量的情況下，實現了1.258倍端到端推理加速，並減少73.94%的提示KV Cache，驗證了該方法在實際部署中的效率優勢。 隨著多模態大模型向高解析度、長上下文、複雜真實場景演進，Token冗餘帶來的算力、視訊記憶體成本問題，已經成為產業規模化落地的核心阻礙。 紫東太初GMC不僅是一款全新的核心集剪枝方法，更提供高效、可信的多模態部署新範式： 視覺壓縮的核心不是減少Token數量，而是以更低的計算代價，完整支撐模型精準推理所需的全域性視覺資訊 。 未來紫東太初大模型團隊將持續迭代GMC技術體系，適配更多大模型架構與複雜業務場景，持續破解多模態模型「算力成本與推理精度」的核心矛盾，推動國產多模態大模型高效、低成本、規模化落地。 title: 2026中國科創投資夏季峰會暨陝西科創產業生態大會圓滿落幕
abstract: 2026中國科創投資夏季峰會暨陝西科創產業生態大會圓滿落幕 量子位的朋友們 2026-08-12 15:31:19 來源： 量子位 2026年7月29日—30日，由融中財經和秦創原科技創新投資集團主辦的2026中國科創投資夏季峰會暨陝西科創產業生態大會圓滿落幕。 當前，全球產業格局正迎來AI驅動與新質生產力引領的系統性重構。 在此背景下，國家頂層設計明確指出未來產業具有前瞻性、戰略性和顛覆性，應因地制宜、錯位發展，推動未來產業與新興產業、傳統產業協同提質。順應這一歷史洪流，投資行業更需以長期主義為底色、以硬科技為錨點深耕產業，在服務產業高質量發展的同時，把握下一輪增長機遇。 2026年7月29日—30日，由融中財經和秦創原科技創新投資集團主辦的2026（第十二屆）中國科創投資夏季峰會（有限合夥人峰會、創新產業峰會）暨陝西科創產業生態大會，在西安香格里拉大酒店隆重啟幕。兩大盛會聯袂舉行，共同打造中國頂級產業生態圈。 作為科教資源重鎮與“硬科技”概念的策源地，陝西正沿著這一方向完成從“科技資源大省”向“科技資本高地”的關鍵躍遷。2026年度省級上市後備企業名單遴選出530家優質企業，僅西安高新區就有170家入選，覆蓋光子資訊、半導體積體電路、生物醫藥、航空航天、新材料、新能源儲能、智慧裝備等核心賽道。制度、資金與專案三端同頻，使陝西成為當下全國優秀創投機構西進佈局的高頻目的地，也讓“科技—產業—金融”的良性迴圈在西部有了可複製的樣本。 2026年，出資人定勢謀遠，出資格局已演變為“產業資本領銜、金融資本發力、國資精準調控”的三元組合新格局；投資人重塑價值，厚積致遠，深潛篤行；在以新質生產力創新的政策指引下，企業綻放力量，破界重構，未來已來。 兩天峰會全面探討投資趨勢、硬科技以及未來產業的發展，打造出資人、投資人和企業端產融生態圈，促進投資產業鏈的融合與貫通。與此同時，還有多場融中生態對接系列活動同步進行。 7月29日，以“定勢”為主題的有限合夥人峰會正式開啟。 陝西省委金融辦常務副主任、省委金融工委常務副書記、省地方金融管理局局長蘇虎超出席並發表致辭。 蘇虎超指出，近年來，陝西先後出臺科技金融50條、資本市場改革16條，探索形成了以科技金融“五項機制”改革為一體，以科創基金整合重組、傳統金融改造升級為兩翼的科技金融“一體兩翼”架構。針對行業普遍關注的容錯機制等問題，探索推出分級容虧制度，創投子基金最高容虧率50%、種子天使類最高70%。截至6月末，全省科技貸款餘額9782.02億元，科創基金叢集總規模破千億元，撬動社會資本近800億元；全省A股上市公司85家，2026年省級上市後備企業530家，其中科技型企業佔比97.36%。陝西作為科教大省、國家區域科技創新中心，科創基因深厚、產業基礎堅實。下一步，陝西將持續完善創投配套服務、儲備優質科創專案、深化與全國各類資本深度合作，誠邀創投機構深耕陝西，共享硬科技發展機遇。 隨後，融中集團董事長朱閃發表了主辦方致辭。 朱閃全面總結了2026年上半年中國股權投資市場的執行態勢，結合長週期行業業績基準研判發展規律，並圍繞本土創投生態構建與陝西科創投資機遇展開了深度分享。朱閃表示，“頭部機構對明星專案‘聯合押注’形成共識，區域上長三角領跑、珠三角與京津冀活躍、成渝緊隨、西部潛力巨大。”他同時表示，“團隊追蹤2013—2024年間2233只人民幣基金真實表現，構建了行業業績基準，核心結論是：基金表現與設立年份及產業週期密切相關，單一指標不足以評價基金，相同條件下基金間表現差距顯著。” 對於中國創投行業未來，朱閃提出三個判斷：第一，人民幣基金時代才剛剛開始，最終格局應是“國資+市場化+本土化美元基金”的組合；第二，LP的成熟是GP成熟的先決條件，未來幾年LP的進化速度將決定整個行業的進化速度；第三，獨立第三方機構的進化速度將決定行業迭代發展與資訊效率，誰能幫助GP與LP降低摩擦、提升透明度，誰就能拿到行業賦能平臺的門票。 緊接著，長安匯通集團黨委書記、董事長、秦創投董事長陶峰發表主辦方致辭。 陶峰表示，本次大會依託陝西獨特的區位、科教及產業優勢，聚焦產業創新、智創未來核心主題，搭建了政產企研融協同交流合作平臺。 他進一步介紹，作為省級科技金融平臺，秦創原科技創新投資集團持續完善科創基金體系、深化科技金融改革、匯聚優質產業資本。本次與融中財經攜手辦會，旨在深挖陝西科創發展機遇、連結全國優質資源、健全區域科創生態，助力陝西科技自立自強與科技強省建設。 在主旨演講環節， 國際貨幣基金組織（IMF）原副總裁朱民圍繞《中國科技走向世界：機遇和挑戰》進行了主旨演講。 朱民表示，中國科技出海正依託製造業與人工智慧的深度融合構建新的競爭優勢，但全球經濟已進入地緣政治定價的新階段，風險結構從經濟金融變數轉向地緣政治不確定性，中國企業需要在做強自身技術與製造根基的同時，依託專業、可信、高質量的第三方服務，才能真正把握這一輪科技出海的歷史機遇。 全國社保基金理事會原副理事長王忠民發表了以《優秀LP的交易結構長啥樣？》為主題的主旨演講。 王忠民指出，面對未來產業的高度不確定性，LP交易結構不是規避風險的工具，而是擔當風險、管理風險的制度鑰匙。他以“無限風光在險峰”概括第一重邏輯——風險必須被ALL IN；以“界觀世界”概括第二重邏輯——交易結構是連線微觀企業與宏觀產業的解析層；以“交易結構穿透無數次摺疊”概括第三重邏輯——每一層市場摺疊都將投資能力放大一個量級。 他認為，從國家產業引導基金到母基金，從母基金到專業基金，LP身份的穿透使得風險厭惡型資本也能投向社會經濟發展最前沿的領域。而差異化的股權交易結構，從同股同權到不同股不同權不同利，則讓創新力量發揮到極致。最終，一級市場的交易創新通過註冊制等制度“摺疊”到二級市場，使公眾資本和社會資本得以分享時代紅利。 在當天上午的圓桌論壇上，普華資本、中科創星、工銀資本、上海國投先導、浙創產業、秦創投、匯通投資、唐興資本、國新基金、上海浦東科創集團海望資本、上海航空產業基金、福田資本運營集團、武創投集團、洪山科投集團、廣州金控基金等機構投資人圍繞“產投同頻，新興產業賽道下國資與市場化資本的生態共建”“穿越週期，耐心資本的配置邏輯與退出再平衡” 展開了兩場精彩的討論。 在下午的會議上，長安匯通集團黨委副書記、總經理焦振華以《耐心資本如何“耐心”——來自陝西的實踐》為題進行了主題推介。 他表示，當前中國科創投資邁入硬科技主導、長期主義盛行的全新週期。 陝西憑藉科技、教育、產業優勢，依託科創科技成果轉化“三項改革”、科技型企業發展“四個工程”、科技金融服務“五項機制”改革，充分釋放科技創新、產業創新、金融服務創新疊加融合的綜合效能，加快提升全要素生產率，創新驅動高質量發展取得紮實成效。秦創投立足本土科創生態，構建了“基金與直投雙擎驅動、策源與服務雙重支撐”的業務佈局，從創新策源、中試賦能、產學研協同、科技金融服務、推動創新制度落地等多方面完善科創生態。 焦振華表示，秦創投秉持開放共享共建理念，呼籲各界深化資源、技術、資本全域合作，攜手啟用陝西硬科技勢能，共創科創產業共贏新生態。 接下來，融中財經重磅釋出了《量子九龍圖》。 這是融中依託“星宿圖”產業圖譜體系，首次以“九龍圖”形式對中國量子產業核心力量進行系統性梳理，為行業帶來了一份清晰呈現產業格局、技術脈絡與核心企業的全景圖譜。 在當天下午的圓桌論壇上，來自華義創投、浦耀信曄、創東方投資、海願資本、尚頎資本、江西江投資本、江西江投基金、基石創投、萬林國際、善達投資、初芯集團、西高投、乾融資本、龍鼎投資、國科嘉和、元禾璞華、永鑫方舟、一村資本、澳銀資本、凱聯資本、西安財金基金公司、雄安基金等機構的嘉賓圍繞“量子、核聚變、腦機，未來產業走入無人區”“算力時代下半導體產業升級與生態構建”“如何從單向募資走向LP與GP的價值共創”等話題展開討論，進行了一場場精彩的思想碰撞。 與此同時， 29日大會期間，中國母基金第十一屆輞川論道圓滿舉辦， 本屆輞川論道邀請了來自各大金融機構、國有資本平臺、政府引導基金、市場化母基金等機構出席，旨在為投資機構分析行業大勢、論道資本創新的專業交流平臺。 7月30日，以“破局”為題的創新產業峰會正式啟幕。 會議伊始， 北京大學教授、深圳國際量子研究院院長俞大鵬以《萬物皆可量子——量子計算、人人有責》為題發表了主旨演講。 他從“萬物皆可量子”出發，系統闡釋了量子力學作為宇宙萬物底層執行規律的科學基礎。他指出，第一次量子革命推動了半導體、雷射、核能、CT等技術發展，奠定了現代自動化、資訊化和第三次工業革命的基礎。當前，經典計算面臨物理極限，資料規模持續增長，加之量子操控能力不斷提升，正共同推動第二次量子革命加速發展。與此同時，量子計算仍面臨量子位元操控精度不足、錯誤率較高、技術路線尚未收斂等難題，需要科研、工程、產業和資本各方共同參與。未來三至五年，量子產業有望湧現出一批高成長企業。 深創投集團黨委委員、副總裁王新東圍繞《風險投資助力新質生產力發展》進行了主旨演講。 他指出，中國科技創新正由跟跑、並跑加快邁向部分領域領跑，產業競爭也從模式創新轉向原始創新和技術驅動。面對人工智慧、量子科技、核聚變、腦機介面等前沿產業較長的工程化和商業化週期，風險投資需要重塑研投一體的認知力、產業賦能的組織力、全週期陪伴的定力和合規經營的約束力四項核心能力，從追逐估值價差轉向創造長期價值。同時，應進一步完善政府引導基金考核讓利、國資創投盡職免責和多元退出機制，引導更多資本投早、投小、投長期、投硬科技。 隨後， 洪泰基金創始合夥人、董事長盛希泰帶來了以《AI時代中國資本市場的結構性變革》為題的主旨演講。 盛希泰以長鑫科技2026年7月登頂A股市值榜首為標誌性事件，揭示市場新舊動能全面切換的趨勢。硬科技成為行情核心主線，算力、光通訊、儲存等賽道企業盈利實現數倍爆發，行情依託真實產業利潤支撐，脫離了單純的題材炒作。 同時，他認為當下A股市值天花板持續抬升，萬億級科技企業批次湧現，市場演進邏輯逐步對標美股。盛希泰表示，這場變革帶來了多層分化：區域上創新資源向東部核心城市集聚；行業間AI賽道與傳統產業景氣度懸殊；企業端輕資產技術型公司價值遠超重資產傳統巨頭；個體層面對AI的認知差距拉開發展層級。整體來看，AI驅動新質生產力重塑資本定價規則，深耕硬核技術、把握產業長期趨勢的主體將佔據時代發展主動權。 接下來， 崑崙萬維董事長兼CEO方漢進行了題為《內容越多，什麼越貴？》的主旨演講。 他表示，AIGC正在大幅降低影像、影片和音樂的生產成本，但內容供給越充足，優質內容、版權資產、穩定交付能力和使用者分發渠道反而越稀缺。對投資者而言，不能只看模型榜單、呼叫價格和內容生成數量，更要關注可用內容的實際成本、商業化效率、版權合規及交易閉環。其中，影像賽道重在工作流與商用授權，影片賽道重在穩定生產管線和可用鏡頭成本，音樂賽道則重在版權、藝人合作和分發機制。未來真正具有投資價值的，不是簡單生成內容或呼叫模型的公司，而是能夠控制內容生產、權利和分發交易閉環的企業。 在當天上午的圓桌論壇上，浙科投資、浙創投、臨芯投資、達晨財智、鼎暉投資、杭實資管、國泰海通、美團龍珠、上海天使會、極佳視界、九識智慧、九章雲極、星動紀元、望石智慧等機構與企業圍繞“非共識捕獵，硬科技投資的確定性主線”“技術商業化時代，獨角獸的成長密碼”展開了精彩的討論。 在下午的會議上，澳銀資本創始合夥人、董事長熊鋼以《迴歸風險投資的本質》發表了主旨演講。 他指出，風險投資本質上是一場圍繞技術創新和不確定性的機率博弈，投資機構需要理解技術演進規律，把握不同階段的投資機率，並通過專業能力提升獲取超額收益。熊鋼以澳銀資本23年的美元母基金和人民幣基金實踐為例，分享了兩類基金在投資邏輯、回報表現和退出機制上的差異。他表示，美元母基金通過分散配置優質GP、依靠長期資本和成熟退出機制取得了較好回報，而人民幣股權投資仍面臨退出難等挑戰。對於風險投資而言，投資只是過程，退出才是最終檢驗，GP需要持續提升識別價值、管理風險和實現退出的能力。
